title: [2018.1.3] [Bug/Feedback] White video screens until all videos have loaded.
details:
After doing some testing with the new video sync update I am very happy that it has improved so much and doesn't cause any lag when loading into worlds with videos, especially the ones with many.

However, the worlds with many videos in it, will have a white screen until all videos have loaded before it syncs up.

So worlds with a lot of videos can for some people seem like the video player isn't working.

There was also the issue, where the video sync only starts for one player, even when multiple people joined into the room at the same time.

Would it be possible to prioritize the synced index to load first and play once loaded, while the rest are loading in the background?

https://youtu.be/bGeqCe0y4Wk

00:00 - 07:00 -  Video player only starts for one user. But changing the video index fixes it.

07:00 - 12:00 - Videos are loaded, but white screen so very unsure if the video player starts or not. But instant play when Task Manager shows that Youtube-dl has finished.

12:00 - 16:00 - Still have to wait for all videos to load in the background before anything happens, but syncs up for people with slower connections.

17:00 - 23:00 - Hiding the video panel makes the video stop, only way to get it started again is to have the master client also hide & show the video player.
Also, video doesn't sync when it is hidden from you when you load in (intended?) 

23:00 - Have to wait for videos to load before anything can be played. (intended?)


Don't have much expertise in this, but if it could allow us to play the synced index as soon as it has loaded then load the rest it the background it would be great!

title: [2018.2.1][Feedback] Remove Favorite Friend Icon on Nameplates
details: In its current state, the favorite friend system has large potential for drama between people. The ability to bookmark specific friends is very convenient, but displaying this status in the nameplate will lead to jealousy/frustration/misunderstanding when people see their status in screenshots, streams, videos, etc. Referring to this as a bookmark system instead of a favorite system as well would help in reducing the favoritism that comes along with being a "favorite friend".

title: [2018.2.3] [FEEDBACK] VRChat Status
details: As far as I know, users reported that status icons are too big and they look kind of "aggressive" (actually, maybe that's not the right word, but they're just uncomfortable to look at, even though it's just Beta and things like that should be expected). Instead, I suggested using border colors, like on Steam. On the first image below you should be able to see a few examples I made for statuses I'd call "Online", "Idle" (or "Away", but not "AFK"), "Do Not Disturb", "Streaming", and "Join Me", most of which are based on similar options on Discord. Also, while I was coming up with alternatives, my first thought was about the background color, so that's another option as well.

details:

Second, Unity UI with custom URL input field becomes very popular last times, but have some specific setup, works only for master, and also glitches some times. title: [2018.2.3 614][BUG] Reparenting an object from an enabled parent to a disabled parent breaks trigger
details:
Using UI Buttons allows for more complex behavior. One such behavior is passing around a gameobject with an onEnable trigger to change the action for a button without replacing the button. (Simplifying it here) 
Doing this on live works, but on beta this will end up breaking the trigger and then break the parent. 

In the example below, there are two buttons. The left performs an action, but by default does nothing. When you press the right button it enables a sphere, and allows the left button to turn it off. 
When you press these buttons the first time, it works. The second time, the child object gets a Deferred event warning and does not activate. The third time, both the child and the parent get the deferred event warning and do not activate. Deferred event warnings no longer show in 614 though.

https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/449386885299830794/480176231694991410/Broken_triggers_on_reparent.unitypackage

title: Full body tracking broken with NullReferenceException in VRCVrIkController
details:
Apologies for the long report. This is a bit of a weird bug, but it seems to be new in this latest beta version build 634 (as of 2018-10-02). Might depend on the avatar and/or the order trackers are turned on. It is reproducible on my avatars 

The bug has a few consequences. In addition to spewing exceptions into the output_log (I have included the first such examples at the end), I notice the following symptoms:

- full-body IK tracking works perfectly fine from my perspective, but everybody else sees me as a desktop user (no arm/leg/hip tracking, only head moves around). If I am in the system menu, people see my avatar frozen in place even if I am moving.

- animations, such as walking, crouching, prone do not work from my perspective when using 3P Holoport or d+pad movement. My avatar freeze poses completely and looks like it is gliding while using movement, even if prone. Other players see me walking normally

- emotes work for me but appear as if they are additive against my full body pose. For example, backflip looks like I am doing a high kick and some emotes cause my legs to float off the ground, even ones that shouldn't be moving the legs. Other people see my emotes normally.

I was able to restore full motion by turning all my trackers on again (may have had to try twice) and switching avatars again. title: [SOLVED]Extra IK Solvers with Execution Order are always on, cannot be turned off
details:
EDIT: The below behavior is explained by IK Execution Order completely overriding the way the IK solvers execute. This can be worked around by disabling your avatar's execution order and enabling your own (on a separate object), or by *only* defining the VR IK component in the execution order. Final IK has undocumented behavior where other IK solvers will implicitly solve after anything defined in execution order.

The current open beta seems to have fixed the issue where additional IK solvers would make your footsteps act strangely.

However, I can now no longer turn off my IK solvers (such as extra FABRIK components) when using IK Execution Order. Even if I disable the FABRIK component or disable the target object, the solver remains on.

If I move the FABRIK script to another disabled object, the FABRIK solver still remains on. If I *also* move the IK Execution Order script to this new object, the FABRIK becomes toggle-able, but also makes my avatar tap their feet very rapidly (like the old behavior).

comments.value:
After some more testing, it seems this canny post can be closed.

This behaviour seems to be the *intended* way for IK Execution Order to work. You can apparently turn your own solvers on/off by not including them in execution order, which will make them implicitly execute later on. You can also have a disabled execution order on another object containing VR IK and your own solver, and simply toggle between the two.
At user request, I'm closing this ticket, but leaving it as Complete rather than Closed so it is easier to find.

title: Increase default limit to 50
details:
Public world optimization guidelines dictate that you may not have more than 50 dynamic bone transforms.

Please consider increasing the default limit to 50 transforms. The config file is hard enough to edit for newer players as it is, and they will be left wondering why a lot of the public avatars they choose will lack physics entirely.

comments.value:
The limit was chosen to line up with the maximum limits per the "Medium" ranking.

The Avatar World Performance Scan numbers were created before the Avatar Stats ranking system was implemented. In reality, the scan's limits should actually _drop_ to the Medium ranking's limits, but it felt as if that would pull the rug out from under many public avatar world creators at the time.
This post is being closed as the limit will not be changed to 50 per the OP's request.

comments.mergedPostDetails:
Trigger OnDisable doesn't work properly when the gameobject gets disable. this problem has appeared in VRChat 2019.2.1 open beta.

I put 3 cubes on a plane here, and Cube 2 and 3 are disable at first. Cube 1 can turn Cube 2 enable and disable as I interact it. When Cube 2 gets enable, Cube 3 also turns enable since Cube 2 has a VRC_trigger component fired by OnEnable. However, when Cube 2 gets disabled, Cube 3 doen't disappear although Cube 2 has a trigger OnDisable.

details:
(Though I already posted to discord open-beta-discussion, I report here again for not forgotten.)

I tested OnTimer trigger issues I reported before with build 741. I think this fix is done in incomplete way. As release notes said, my example is "not set to Repeat". But I think this setup must be reusable even if "not set to Repeat".
I guess the maintainer thought: "non Repeat" means "it is one-shot timer" so it fires no more than once. But this setup use "Reset On Enable". OnTimer document says "Reset On Enable" means "If true the timer will be reset". IMO, this "reset" should include resetting a state of "it already fired (or not) as one-shot timer". (And then, it will be reusable.)
If current fix is correct, OnTimer document should explain different meaning of "reset" in "Repeat" and "Reset On Enable" parameters. I think that will be a source of confusion.

(original report: https://vrchat.canny.io/bug-reports/p/ontimer-reset-on-enable-does-not-reset-its-started-time )
title: [2019.2.1] [741] OnTimer with "Repeat"=off shoud be reusable if "Reset On Enable"=on

comments.value:
I will clarify for Naqtn, in case his language is difficult to understand. 

What I believe he is saying, is that Repeat should not be tied to Reset On Enable. Repeat means it fires after every time interval. Reset On Enable means that OnEnable, the timer starts from 0 and does the action once, even if it had already been done once in the instance. If the object is disabled and the-enabled, without Repeat on, it should act as a “fresh” timer. It should NOT require Repeat to work.
Fixed in build 744, now on Open Beta. The "Repeat" flag is reset if ResetOnEnable is enabled.

details:
This issue has already been reported, but I figured it'd be best to post here too for others. 

Currently in the beta branch, using Index/Knuckles controllers on a hybrid setup(Oculus + Lighthouse) does not allow the user to take advantage of the new finger tracking system. It does, however, seem to work with Windows Mixed Reality + Lighthouse hybrid setups, so that's great! While I understand that hybrid setups are not an officially supported setup within VRChat, a number of users do currently use it for full body tracking on non-lighthouse headsets.  

For Rift hybrids in particular, being able to use Index controllers in VRChat ontop of FBT is advantageous, as the Rift Touch controllers cause IR interference with any device tracking with lighthouse technology, even 2.0 devices(Rift users in FBT have much more frequent hip flyoff than other FBT users due to this). Because of this, I'd expect many hybrid-setup users to pick up Index controllers for that benefit, as well as being able to track their fingers. 

Hopefully there's an easy fix for this, even if it's not technically a bug!

Edit for the sake of more information: As Index controllers currently are on Rift-hybrid setups, they are treated as Touch controllers within VRChat.
title: [785] - Index Support on Hybrid Setups

comments.value: my thoughts go back to the moon dust demo game. You didnt have to squeeze to pick up items just had to close your hand. How it currently works with sqeezing to pick up is nice so you dont accidently pickup items when you close your hand. But for dark worlds where you have to constantly hold on to a flashlight. Peoples hands will gradually loosen over time and will accidently drop the item. So you could have squeezing to pickup but not dropping until you do open hand.
Right now the gripping value seems like it's a little high. Holding something for a long period of time without accidentally dropping it would get pretty exhausting. :)

I agree with this, but I also think you should not have to grip the controllers at all in order to grab items. From people who've played games like Boneworks or Moondust with the Index controllers, they say it is a lot more immersive to grab using the mechanic of closing their hands around the controllers instead of gripping, as the rest position of your hand on the controllers are supposed to be open hand anyway.

I'm marking this as complete due to the fact that in 2019.2.3's latest build, you now have the choice (via SteamVR's Controller Bindings) to handle object grabbing via "Grip Release" or "Open Hand Release", which behaves a bit like you've described. Try both!

title: Not to do the hard poly limit  (oculus quest)

comments.value: I vouch and have proof with a world that has such avatars.

If you can get 10 avatars on screen with high poly counts in a quest world like the home world or hub, reaching 72fps with smooth frame times, then I would believe you. Until then these restrictions are necessary on both platforms.

VR software does a lot to compensate for low frame rates and the quest is no exception. Everything my appear smooth but you would not be hitting a high enough frame rate for the optimal experience and the frame timings would be resulting in an unstable frame rate or stutter.

In addition to all this, even if the poly count did perform well, developing an app for the oculus quest has some recommendations and guidelines that vrchat are keeping as close to as they can.

Quest limitations (on all components, not just polygons) are set for implementation in the next release. Although I understand the frustration, this is required to ensure good performance and a good experience on the Quest.

details:
Multiple Oculus audio scripts were removed from the dependencies folder of VRChat's SDK in this version.

One of the removed scripts was `ONSP Ambisonics Native` -- this script was historically required to decode ambisonic audio properly alongside Unity's native support. [It seems to still be the case according to the Oculus docs.](https://developer.oculus.com/documentation/audiosdk/latest/concepts/ospnative-unity-ambisonic/#add-ambisonic-audio-to-a-unity-scene)

I'm unsure of how many world creators are currently using ambisonics in their world, but removing this script could result in some audio chaos when they update their world with the new SDK. The ability to have ambisonic audio in worlds should remain either way! 

If anyone is unsure of what ambisonics is, it basically allows you to create a sphere of 3D audio packed into a single audio file. It's becoming a standard format in VR for looping ambient environment sounds, music cues, etc. [Here's some other nerd info on it!](https://www.waves.com/ambisonics-explained-guide-for-sound-engineers)

details:
The current iteration of `VRC_SpatialAudioSource` has the default gain level set to 10. Because this component ~currently~ seems to act as a conduit for ONSP Audio Source, this means you're driving the audio source 10db hotter than unity gain. 

The default gain should be set to 0...and maybe even have the gain level option removed from the `VRC_SpatialAudioSource` to avoid confusion/redundancy. This would ensure that gain staging is managed by Unity's audio source component exclusively. Otherwise, what people hear in their editor may be louder at runtime.

This has been a long-standing thing, but it's more important to squash this now with the addition of limiting/compression on the master bus where 10db can cause audio to pass the compression threshold.
title: [w_2019.2.5] [802] [SDK Feedback] Gain should be set to 0 and not 10 by default

comments.value: 100% agree. This game already has a loudness problem, this will just make the problem worse
The other options should be set to what the global default for the world is too. So you have it as a reference​ point to start from.

We received complaints and feedback when voices were at 15db gain. So, we added an additional 6db gain to the voice in build 803. That means regular audio at 10db default gain is already significantly lower than voice.

Changing the default to 0 would cause default audio to be far lower than voice (and way too quiet overall).

We won't be changing this for now.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Are you saying VOIP was peaking at -15db in the mix or that y'all were driving the VOIP group +15db for balance? 

I obviously respect the decision to not change anything for now if it's gonna affect the experience. But ~long-term~ for feedback-sake, I think there might be a misunderstanding where the gain setting is being seen as a fader instead of an amplifier.

Regular audio with +10db gain added is going to be as quiet or as loud as whatever the input / audio clip peaks at ...plus 10db. This default can be an issue because creators are going to have sources + clips that peak at varying levels (or some may even normalize peaks to 0db so they can do levels in Unity). So rhetorically, if they have an audio clip that's peaking at 0db with their volume set to 1; the added 10db gain means they're now clipping 10db. (っ °Д °;)っ Additionally, that 10db overdrive will definitely pass the master bus compression threshold depending on a player's volume settings. 

Obviously feel free to take this with a grain of salt, but possibly a better option to try out would be to be cut rather than amplify. By that I mean, balance the game's overall mix out by only lowering volume even if it means everything is globally quieter. You'll have your balanced game mix with a bit of headroom - so on the master bus, you can simply add gain/amplify once to hit your desired loudness + use the newly-added compressor to tame any crazy transients. You'd have better staging + dynamics, and there shouldn't be a need to amplify anything on our end by default for balance!

Hi @bd_, thanks for the feedback!

We did not add explicit support for dynamically changing the collider area. If the values are animated, it is unexpected behaviour.

VRC_VoiceRegionOverride is based on Trigger (Collider) callbacks. If you make changes to it while a player is inside the trigger, the changes won't apply until the player leaves and re-enters. There's currently a fade between enabled and disabled falloff, so the transition is smoother but we aren't sure what the expected sound behaviour would be for a changing collider.

What is the use case for animating VRC_VoiceOverrideRegions trigger colliders?

@{58c62e995865713647a7115b|full_name}: In my case I was originally trying to set up something where I could adjust parameters in real time to better understand what they do. If this isn't intended to be supported, please put a note to this effect in the documentation.

Note also that I was specifically animating the VoiceOverrideRegion parameters, not the collider itself.

Animating the enable/disable state itself, or moving the collision region, would be useful as it can be used to simulate more complex behavior - eg having two rooms side by side but preventing you from hearing the other side by forcing the far range to zero for the room you're not in, or having a small region follow a specific player.. Last I tested, animating enable/disable state worked, but I haven't tested moving the region.

@{5c1475afb7ce126e9e0e3a39|full_name}: Moving the collision region should be supported, as should enabling/disabling the region itself. (update Jul 25: This is not correct, and enabling/disabling the region is NOT supported. See comments below, and our docs.)

I have added notes regarding the non-support of changes to the SpatialAudioSource and VoiceOverrideRegion properties at run-time.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: `as should enabling/disabling the region itself.`

Is this still true after the testing discussion last night?

@{58c6cbcffd04b1785f747b6c|full_name}: Nope, that's changed. Per our docs, enabling/disabling the region (gameObject or component) isn't supported and is discouraged. This is due to the behavior of the Unity onExitTrigger event.

We encourage users to move regions that need to be toggled on/off into the floor or otherwise out of the way via an animation.

Due to the way PlayerAudioOverride is applied, animating the properties isn't supported and will not work. Instead, we recommend setting up multiple regions with the varying settings you wish to have available. When you want to swap these regions, move the trigger collider into position using an animation.

We explicitly do not support enabling/disabling the region (gameObject or component). This is due to the behavior of the Unity onTriggerExit event.

comments.value:
In 805, audio falls as 1/d^2 where d is the distance from the source. If the Far value is x, voice cutoff occurs at 0.5*x. 

There is an additional interpolation that occurs from 0.25*x to 0.5*x that drops audio intensity to 0. This is to prevent a sharp cut-off at the 0.5*x distance.

Default voice Far value is set to 80m, so by default the hard-limit is 40m. Following the inverse-square, audio at 40m is 1/1600th of the original intensity, and is essentially inaudible.

Please read about the reasoning behind this here: https://docs.vrchat.com/v2019.2.5/docs/vrc_voiceoverrideregion#section-vrchat-falloff-curve-adjustments

details:
I understand that you've limited the far distance of avatar audio sources, forced them to an inverse square falloff, and forced near/volumetric radius to zero to ensure that they actually get quieter as you move away. This is all well and good and should hopefully reduce problems with very loud avatars - however, when designing an avatar that is intended to not cause a disturbance to others nearby it presents a conundrum - if you set the maximum value for far radius, you'll potentially disturb people far away, but if you set it to be short, then falloff is unnaturally sharp for people nearby. This may also cause issues for audio sources that are specifically designed to only be audible very close to their origin (heartbeat effects, for example), as now the audio volume will change quite rapidly with any small change in distance from the source.

To help address these issues, please provide a way that avatar audio sources can use a gradual falloff nearby, then transition to a falloff curve sharper than normal at a configurable distance. This could be designed to be no louder than the maximum distance falloff curve used in the beta currently.

Changes are in progress.

Going forward, if you set Far Limit to 0 (or less) you will mute all avatar sources within that VRC_PlayerAudioOverride.

A Far Limit with really small values will probably sound different with and without ONSP applied, this is normal and expected. 

Setting the Gain to negative, as before, mutes avatar audio. This is true whether or not ONSP is applied, and this is probably what most users would use.

Regardless, we strongly recommend using a VRC_SpatialAudioSource with all audio sources on avatars.

@{5b2821f1443b6a55287c67ad|full_name}: Boop, update because I was being dumb about the reason here since I was incorrectly assuming the Quest client was built using IL2CPP and would have the same issues if this was due to IL2CPP. But the Quest client is apparently using Mono at the moment, so this is the first time IL2CPP has reared its head.

The UI issue ends up being unrelated to the issue at hand since it still functions fine as long as you can get the event bound properly. Unity marked the OnValueChanged event with a float argument as private in 2018 which had the side effect of breaking the UI for it. The slider UI issue is a UI problem which I was able to fix in my custom event editor with the same fix Unity did.

I made a project to test the issue and try to reproduce it, and it looks like this ends up being due to IL2CPP stripping unused functions as TCL also suspected.

Just wanted to correct myself on the point with the sliders since the UI issue is unrelated. Most stuff past this point I assume is already known/being worked on but is included for completeness.

My test scene consisted of a slider on a canvas setup to call Rebind() and Update() on an animator via OnValueChanged the color of the slider to red. This is what it is supposed to look like: https://i.imgur.com/7BYCTKb.mp4

If I put the slider in the scene normally, it works fine in editor play mode, Mono backend builds, and IL2CPP backend builds. However, if I package the slider into an asset bundle and load it through StreamingAssets at runtime, the IL2CPP build does not work. If I make a slider in the scene that is hidden, but calls the same Rebind() and Update() functions, then the IL2CPP build that loads the slider from StreamingAssets will work since IL2CPP know knows that the functions are used.

Most games will not run into issues like this when using IL2CPP since Unity will scan through UI events like the slider OnValueChanged callback to look at what functions they reference at build time of the client. This requires Unity to be aware of all the levels and content in those levels. In VRChat's case, you use asset bundles of content that other people make so the IL2CPP compiler can't know what functions they reference.

IL2CPP code stripping is likely what is also breaking player tracking v2 and other prefabs in worlds.

The IL2CPP code stripping only applies to builtin Unity types and external assemblies you import. So most things in the world whitelist such as standard asset scripts and FinalIK are not affected since they are part of the main assembly.

Unity provides a way to prevent stripping of methods, properties, fields, and events without needing to generate stubs via link.xml which is documented here: https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/IL2CPP-BytecodeStripping.html

I added a basic link.xml to the root of the Assets folder that forces the IL2CPP compiler to include all of the functions on UnityEngine.Animator. This fixed the slider in my case and allowed me to use the slider in IL2CPP without including something that uses the functions on the animator.

This was the basic link.xml (with no indenting because I don't know how to make canny respect it):
<linker>
    <assembly fullname="UnityEngine">
            <type fullname="UnityEngine.Animator" preserve="all"/>
    </assembly>
</linker>

You’d probably want to add most of the builtin UnityEngine types in the world whitelist to link.xml to prevent worlds from breaking. But if there are specific functions on the whitelisted types that pose a concern you could preserve specific functions within a type, though you obviously can’t use those functions in the code base or Unity would re-add them.

The bytecode stripping documentation has more examples, but this is a version of link.xml that fixes the slider specifically without including the entirety of the Animator class as an example:

<linker>
    <assembly fullname="UnityEngine">
        <type fullname="UnityEngine.Animator" preserve="nothing">
            <method name="Update"/>
            <method name="Rebind"/>
        </type>
    </assembly>
</linker>

Of course there are a lot of other functions on Animators and other whitelisted components that are used by worlds. So dropping down into the per-function preserving might want to be considered a blacklist within a whitelist to be used only when there’s a problematic function. Especially since you can easily accidentally end up breaking content that uses private functions which are usable using animation events on animations and via buttons using my Easy Event Editor editor script. An example of content that makes use of private functions to be usable is HardLight’s Player Tracking v2 and a lot of prefabs that manually call functions that will often be private like Update, LateUpdate, and Start to work properly.

When you’re adding types to preserve I’d request that you add the RenderTexture and CustomRenderTexture types to that list since more complex shader-based worlds such as SCRN’s “The Home Arcade” world call functions on those to have control over their update loops and bindings. The reason I ask for these specifically is because they are considered assets, and not components so they are not in the component whitelist for worlds and they may be missed, though they have been used in worlds for a while.

Here’s a link to the project files if you want to look at them. It has a thrown-together script to generate the asset bundles and load them for testing. This is made in 2018.4.10 since I couldn’t find 2018.4.9 with the IL2CPP compilation dependencies because of how Unity Hub acts. https://drive.google.com/file/d/1K1A1cxeHqVvGcY5sMyO3mvApOZPyU5NM/view?usp=sharing
Unity states this was fixed in 2018.4.10f1. Is it possible for someone to verify?

details:
The ParticleSystemForceField component new to Unity 2018, combined with "external forces" module can open up a whole new breadth of avatar/world interactions not seen since Ik controlled GPU Particles.

Mimi made an example showing what this component can do: https://i.imgur.com/yglb74H.gifv

For the module to be useful, it must be allowed on avatars so that (combined with IKFollower) leg and arm positions can emit forces. Doing so can enable new types of 30dof interactions not seen before between avatars or between avatars and particle systems in worlds.

Worlds that wish to block avatar particle interactions must only uncheck avatar layers including Player, MirrorReflection etc. For this reason it should be safe to allow avatars to carry this component without impeding world creation.

https://docs.unity3d.com/2018.4/Documentation/Manual/class-ParticleSystemForceField.html

details:
https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/Constraints.html

This system seems to be far better suited to perform a lot of task previously accomplished with other comments, while providing additional options for avatar creators

Allows limb copying without fixed joints (allowing avatars with multiple arms or legs)

Allows using world particles in situations that IKFollower doesn’t allow (Attach to non-IK-following bone) that previously required fixed joints

I believe these allow you to Animate holstering / unholstering weapons without needing to duplicate the mesh (IIRC, FinalIK supported this)

Aim/LookAt constraints can be used to replicate hydraulics pistons or other mechanical joints for robotic avatars (previously this could be achieved with dynamic bones any maybe FinalIK) These components likely can be used to achieve other effects.

These components hopefully won’t have the disadvantages of the systems they replace, such as;
IKFollower: only allowed on IK-following bones (As per documentation)
Rigid Bodies: Known to break in Combat enabled worlds (https://vrchat.canny.io/bug-reports/p/avatar-rigid-bodies-break-in-combat-enabled-worlds)
Rigid Bodies: Some configurations of joints can drift out of place over time or during teleports.

comments.value:
This is going to be marked with "Won't Fix".

We limit per-object data use in order to avoid saturating connections. In this case, the synced animation data is too large-- the parameter names may be too long, or there may be too many parameters.

If you're seeing this message in your output logs, reduce the size of the synced data by shortening parameter names, or reducing the number of parameters synced on that object.

Is it possible that we could get a more solid number of what is acceptable and what is not acceptable? Are we talking 5 parameters, 20, 100? There are usually plenty of methods to reduce even the most complex systems down to under 20, but if we're on a limit of something like 5 then that's really rough.

details:
In the current open beta, systems that use TeleportPlayer to find the player’s play space origin or move players with custom locomotion will usually cause remote clients to look jittery when moving. This can be seen in the videos in this canny. https://feedback.vrchat.com/open-beta/p/874climbing-teleportplayer-3-times-per-frame-breaks-for-vr


Of course, the TeleportPlayer action should be capable of teleporting a player remotely so that we don’t see people fly across the world if they are teleporting from one point to another. But there are numerous popular worlds using the interpolated teleport for player root tracking, climbing, and other player locomotion which are broken from the interpolation bug fix. 


Since both behaviors are desirable in different circumstances, it would be useful to have an option on the TeleportPlayer action after the Align Room To Destination option called “Remote Interpolate Teleport” or something along those lines. This would default to false, and when enabled prevent the local client from telling the remote clients that it has teleported. 


This should allow climbing worlds to fix their content by enabling the remote interpolation option on the teleport actions and re-uploading.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: I found a fairly consistent testcase to demonstrate the non-pickup "object sleeping" issue...and also a really urgent one because it's going to degrade a lot of worlds with QvPen, at least when drawing certain letters.... since its widespread distribution at Vket 3, the QvPen has raced to become the most popular pen prefab in new worlds.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Go to my QVPen world from two clients, and make sure at least one is desktop: https://www.vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_1483ac2f-bae4-464c-a33c-4c456bc48dd7
2. Pick up a pen.
3. For each V shape we draw, click and hold down the mouse: this is to ensure that there is sufficient time for the "start drawing" trigger to broadcast and rule out timing issues there.
4. Quickly move the mouse in a V shape, but not so quickly that the IK gets lost. You should be able to see the pen move in the V shape on the other client.
5. Wait at least a second before releasing the mouse for the same reason: waiting for object sync to interpolate and rule out ordering issues with the "stop drawing" trigger
6. Repeat steps 3-5 as many times as needed for scientific accuracy.

Before getting to my observations let me make a quick note about how QvPen actually works: Each Pen has two object syncs:
- The first object sync is a pickup ("Grip") - this does nothing except visually show the pen and provide ownership.
- The second object sync is called "SpawnTarget": this one uses AutoCam to follow a transform located at the tip of the Grip, and has neither Rigidbody nor Pickup (this combination is what improves reliability in older vrchat versions)

In 2017, you will see the trail actually ahead of the physical pen "Grip", and overall well synced.

In 2018, things are somewhat reversed but also even worse. What I observe in 2018 is that the other client sees the pen move perfectly on time and in the V shape (if you don't see the pen move, you drew v too fast). However...the trail, if it syncs at all, is often over a second behind. Sometimes it is pretty close to the pen. Other times, it just won't go at all.

Note that this bug does not affect some letters like "o" which is a favorite among Desktop users. I believe the shape of the "v" letter somehow improves the likelihood of invoking the object sleeping behavior which causes so much trouble.

In my attached screenshot, you can see the top client seeing very few lines drawn compared to the bottom client that drew them.

comments.value: Before anyone gets mad this is most likely just a simple oversight. VRChat as far as I know is not trying to break texture arrays.

Fixed internally, will be fixed in the next Open Beta version we push.

If you're using Texture Arrays, you should ensure that the textures in use have Texture Mip Map Streaming enabled. The SDK does not check if this is enabled on textures in Texture Arrays, and we consider that best practice for future-proofing and performance reasons.

edit: I didn't know any better, but apparently you cannot enable Mip Map Streaming on generated texture assets-- so you can't enable Mip Map Streaming on Texture Arrays. 🤔

comments.value: Gotta take out that trash!

@{58c6cbcffd04b1785f747b6c|full_name}: It does a GC anyways in the large menu which hitches all over the place already and they didn't need to run GC on quick menu open in 2017. I'm noting a regression which isn't great and would be nice to have fixed since I use my quick menu to check frame rate, emote, look at avatar performance and other stuff somewhat more frequently than I open the main avatar/world/social menu. And if it's not fixed, when someone says a few months from now "but it has always been bad like this" I can point at this issue and tell them it wasn't before a specific patch (this has happened with other bugs in the past). 


IMO they should leave GC to Unity for everything except loading screens since there is next to no determinism when memory will need to be allocated in VRC and manual GC is intended for when you know for a fact when things will need to be allocated for a scene and that they will not need to be freed for a deterministic lifetime. I've seen a few games that had VRC's situation where they were worried about large GC's taking a long time and tried the fix of "but we'll just put a GC here and there and the hitches will be smaller." But the end result of that usually just ends with them putting more hitches in their game because GC has a flat overhead regardless of how much memory actually needs to be cleared. And it turns out that the algorithms made to work fast on billions of devices, with hundreds of thousands of different software packages, generally work better when you let them do their thing instead of going "ah yeah let's put a GC in when you open the quick menu." Normally the answers developers land on are to let the GC do its thing, flatten reference chains, allocate less garbage, or attempt to optimize the GC process itself if they have the resources to do that. If you have an app that has a deterministic pattern to allocating and freeing memory, that's usually the rare case where you know better than the garbage collector. And time spent by VRC attempting to solve GC better than well established algorithms could be better spent on other things until they move to 2019.4 where incremental GC is a thing that mostly solves their issue assuming they aren't churning through enough garbage to stall the incremental GC. If the garbage collection is broken like the periodic hitch canny seemed to indicate last I heard of it, then it's a regression that Unity should be contacted about. Though since enabling logging UI triggers the periodic hitches in the open beta again I guess something in that was causing erroneous GC's that didn't happen in 2017? It would be nice to have the in game logging and info on who's master without sacrificing your performance to the 2018 gods though so I hope that's fixed soon as well. 


But I digress, the issue is under review so hopefully it'll be fixed in the next open beta and I can't even know for certain if it's a GC causing this. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
FYI this continues on build 906.

details:
Unity 2018 now uses the Standard particle shaders by default (e.g. `Particles/Standard Unlit` ), with transparency enabled by default using keyword  _ALPHABLEND_ON/queue override. [edit: `Particles/Standard Surface` is also affected]

The shader does not specify a renderQueue, so it defaults to Geometry (2000). However, most blend settings require Transparent (3000) render queue.

As is widely known but not well documented, be it through a Unity bug or VRChat issue, either the upload or asset bundle load process resets all material renderQueue settings to From Shader. If done to Standard Particle shader, it would cause it to use alpha blending with queue 2000 which looks broken. See attached picture.

Just like Standard, it assigns keywords which can be used to detect the intended renderQueue after upload:
_ALPHABLEND_ON, _ALPHAPREMULTIPLY_ON and _ALPHAMODULATE_ON use Transparent (3000); _ALPHATEST_ON uses AlphaTest (2450)
title: Apply Standard renderQueue fix to Particle/Standard* shaders

details:
Test world ID: https://www.vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_ca7eb52d-b535-4ba6-a947-52d71adb827b

Steps to reproduce:
1. Load with two clients. Be aware of which is master.
2. On Master, hit esc (or in VR, press jump button), click the gear icon, then click any block.
3. On Master, walk outside the blue hatched zone and right click a few times to create blocks. A number will appear each time you click. It should be a number from 1 to 200.
4. On NotMaster, observe that the object sync works, but the number is 765.4321 - this indicates that no trigger executed. The integer part of this number is set using the AnimationFloat trigger. It is directly set on the digit display material from the animation clips.

5. repeat steps 2-4 from NotMaster, and you should observe that both clients see the same number appear.

6. Have Master rejoin.
7. repeat steps 2-4 on either client, and it should continue syncing.

I know this is not boiled down to a simple test case. I am trying to document the behaviour, and also point out that broadcasting triggers *do* work in many cases.

One unusual thing to note: left click (trigger DestroyBlockRemote) does not appear to broadcast the number correctly. One client will see 950 (destroy block ID) and other client will see the old value. I don't know why but I'm assuming this is my own bug since I had to hack up this world last minute to use triggers instead of animation sync.

details:
When existing content is loaded into the Unity 2018-based versions of VRC, materials with a HDR colour will appear incorrect, due to Unity changing how HDR colour values are interpreted. A tool to fix this is now provided in the SDK. 
But for content already uploaded with no other issues, this means updating Unity, resolving new issues caused by the update, and rebuilding data that the Unity editor is no longer compatible with (i.e. LightingData). This is no small task, and a sizeable time investment. 
It would save a lot of effort if VRC's client modified older content when loading to either apply the gamma transform to the colours of materials, or apply the gamma flag to the material properties.
title: [890] Process materials while loading old content to correct colour space

comments.value:
IK isn't the culprit here, that isn't how that data is transferred. Either way:
125 kilobytes/second is way, way below what we expect for a broadband connection (typically defined as 25Mbit). I fully expect a 1Mbit connection to have issues. VRChat is pretty bandwidth-hungry!
Is this a regression from Live? As in, does this issue suddenly occur in Open Beta, but not in Live?

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: I've never noticed it happening in Live before, usually I would just have a high ping due to downloading everyone's avatar and then it was gone while this issue keeps happening even after all the avatars are downloaded. I'll see if I can make a comparison during the week-end.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Something's amiss. Live doesn't use nearly that much upload. Unless this is somehow a bug with some other piece of the networking, it would make sense that the smoother IK improvements would cause this.
Also, as pathetic as a 1 Mbit upload speed is, that's all a large portion of rural US and Canada can get (not to mention the entirety of Australia and anywhere else that isn't metropolitan or Europe). Most people's internet speeds are highly asymmetrical. You may get 25Mbit down, but you're lucky if you get more than a fifth of that up. You're going to hurt a LOT of current VRC players if your attitude is that if they don't have good upload, then fuck them. My ISP is supposed to give me 20Mbit down and 7 up, but in the real world I only get 15-7 down, 3-0.5 up. And that's fairly typical for rural US providers.

@{59cb4676d4edc012b9dca22f|full_name}: I mean they already killed a lot of people with poor internet when they first introduced the networked IK. Previously avatar downloading was an issue for most people so they would just block avatars and be mostly okay. now that is not possible.
I'm lucky here in Australia because I finally got the HFC NBN installed in my area so I'm forced now on 50Mbit down and 20Mbit up. My previous speeds for as long as I can remember were 9Mbit down <1Mbit up and that was painful to play vrchat with even before networked IK.

@{5a55f2c46765067d861f5004|full_name}: Were you able to replicate/make a comparison?
As an additional note, the recommended minimum connection bandwidth for VRChat has always been 25Mbit. This hasn't changed. You can probably do with a bit less, but having a small fraction of that speed will result in very poor bandwidth-related performance.
Due to the nature of how VRChat works, the data it transmits, and the timeliness required by that data to display things in the ways and with the fidelity players desire, there isn't much of a way around it. Bandwidth is bandwidth. Unfortunately, just the way the internet works.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: "the recommended minimum connection bandwidth for VRChat has always been 25Mbit" - That's downstream, this post is about upstream. I would be highly surprised if most people on VRChat had anything near that speed and most of the UK is way below that.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: I haven't been able to make a comparison yet but I will try my best to make one soon. And yeah as mentionned by Enverex this post is about upstream, not downstream. (But I'm assuming you mean 25/3 which is the average ratio)

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: that sounds like a poor excuse. Just because you're forcing one set speed of how things will be downloaded and uploaded does not make it appropriate to push the blame on the user. 
Why does the client not have the option to limit the upload or download for the unnecessary things such as IK when it was a known concern that connections speed would be a problem going forward? 
As indicated the new IK can be tweaked remotely but why were those values not just the maximum that the client could use. Thus allowing the client to limit what would otherwise kill slower speeds. 
You're targeting what seems to be some arbitrary minimum connection speed that you guys need to meet the fidelity we already had or that you promised to achieve, when there should be ways for the clients that can spare the bandwidth to see and send more information for higher fidelity while those that can't will just be interpolated between what they can receive and send.
Effectively if "...the nature of how VRChat works..." was the problem then why was this update to IK not also addressing the bandwidth concerns. There is no way this was not part of the feedback when networked IK was first introduced as everyone knew it would require increasing the data sent and received .
Interesting.
@{5a3ad8ac4a8da67427803715|full_name}: How is this resolved? I'm curious because I'm one of the people who plays with 0.8 Mbps UP.

details:
This issue has existed since the beginning of the 2018 open beta and was very obvious in one of my worlds where I use triggers for basic hierarchical culling. I needed to put together a basic test case for this though.
The basic issue is that on live triggers fire OnExitTrigger when their gameobject gets disabled, since the trigger volume gets disabled as well. This is reliable behavior. 
On open beta, when you disable a gameobject it does not fire OnExitTrigger until the game object is re-enabled. This can cause a bunch of inconsistent behavior.
This is the test world https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_08814acb-a298-4f5f-913b-46233843d143
There are 3 box triggers in this world, each is connected to a VRC_Trigger that enables the next smaller trigger box when you enter one. The 3 boxes in the center show each volume's trigger state. They turn on and off in sequence with each trigger volume you enter and exit.
Walking into and out of the trigger volumes works fine in beta, but if you respawn while inside the center of the the volumes, you will see that some of the volumes have not fired their OnExitTrigger event and have left some of the objects inside enabled. If you respawn from inside all of the triggers in live, everything works as expected and everything gets disabled.
title: [894] Disabled VRC triggers using OnExitTrigger do not fire OnExitTrigger until re-enabled

details:
Currently, it is recommended to do OcclusionCulling when creating a world.
Certainly, OcclusionCulling has reduced the drawing load.
However, hiding undrawn objects can make FPS even better.
This will be difficult to experience in a narrow world.
I am creating a wide open world called Pandora.
Terrain is optimized for Unity2018.
However, with VRC, it seems that the DrawInstanced function that relies on the graphic board for Terrain drawing is not being used 100%.
Despite the fact that the trees planted in large quantities in front are being OcclusionCulling by the mountains,
FPS can be improved by hiding the front terrain by interacting triggers.
In other words, doesn't it mean that even if an object is OcclusionCulling, it only exists there and internal processing is occurring?
OcclusionCulling objects do not need this internal processing.
And when the DrawInstanced feature of Unity 2018's Terrain comes into full effect, VRChat re-opens the door to a fantastic world of imagination.
Please check it.
If you want to test this out, visit the open-beta world I'm working on, Pandora ep.4-Twilight.
A debug switch that hides each area is placed near the spawn point.
This world is still under development. Not published. If you want a World ID, email us.
If you need a better understanding of the world and how it works, we will send you further information via email.
Please consider it.
title: Internal processing and DrawInstanced that impair the effect of OcclusionCulling

details:
Similar to current situation with SDK2 - using an AVPro udon player together with audio effects is not possible

You get the following warning in the log

2020.09.05 01:09:19 Warning    -  Only custom filters can be played. Please add a custom filter or an audioclip to the audiosource (Audio Source).
title: [986] AVPro player ignores LowPass, Reverb and other filters

comments.value:
This is a "can't fix" / "won't fix".
Just like in SDK2, AVPro's audio implementation isn't very robust in regards to how it injects audio. 
As such, this is a limitation of the plugin, and we will not be able to address the issue.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Well, we know tha AVPro itself supports audio filters just fine, so I guess its something about how VRC has it set up, which is unfortunate.
I double checked using the AVPro trial and it played through audio filters via the provided Audio Output component and with the Windows-specific settings set to Unity Audio.
https://streamable.com/fyzreb

@{5c71ea27a884dd22f1960ec2|full_name}: The difference between your setup and VRChat's is that VRChat adds the AVPro AudioOutput component at runtime. This means that it's always the last component on the GameObject so it runs its audio code last. The AVPro AudioOutput component uses OnAudioFilterRead to inject the audio from the MediaPlayer into the AudioSource which since this happens after the other audio filters have run they cannot affect it. Unity doesn't expose any methods for rearranging the order of components at runtime so we can't just move the AudioOutput to be above the filters.

@{5fa30b66b36d4b12af626dc8|full_name}: ok, that's fair, altho i just tested this shitty code for adding at runtime, and it seems like just moving it up and toggling the effects on and off on the same frame - makes it re-apply them
But i guess you can't just shove an internal method without some hacky solutions :thinking: Thanks for details tho! At least it helps to understand what's going on :P

@{5fa30b66b36d4b12af626dc8|full_name}: At this point I guess it'd be more of a feature request, but if you can't reorder the AudioOutput that's created by VRC, it would be nice if we could add an AudioOutput component ourselves. So the AVPro AudioOutput component would need to be whitelisted for SDK3 worlds (it's already whitelisted for SDK2 worlds) and the VRCAVProVideoSpeaker component would need an option to point to a Component reference for the AudioOutput, or a GameObject reference to the game object the AudioOutput  is on to keep the SDK decoupled. The VRCAVProVideoSpeaker would then hook up the AVPro media player that VRC creates at runtime to the AudioOutput.

title: [988] Several important functions missing from UI whitelist

comments.value:
Thanks for capturing these affected worlds and UI requests. The team has reviewed these items and here are our thoughts. Closing this ticket as we'll track the approved items individually.
    *Press*: Couldn't find a matching event, not sure what they're trying to do.
    *SendMessage*: Not allowed since you can use it to call arbitrary messages.
    *BroadcastMessage*: Same as SendMessage.
    *RectTransform.SetParent*: Would need an example of how this is used via UI, seems like a much better candidate for UdonBehaviour.
    *Animator.enabled*: Coming in following release.
    *VRCPickup.PlayHaptics*: Use UdonBehaviour with VRCPickup.PlayHaptics or VRCPlayerApi.PlayHapticEventInHand.
    *Animator.Update*: Need to see an example of how this is used.
    *TextMeshPro.text*: Working on adding TMPro to Udon, will whitelist this method.
    *TextMeshProUGUI.text*: Considering TextMeshProUGUI for inclusion, would be later as it will take more work to implement our UI filtering here as well.
    *UdonBehaviour.OnPickupUseDown*,
    *UdonBehaviour.OnPickupUseUp*,
   *UdonBehaviour.OnStationEntered*,
    *UdonBehaviour.OnStationExited*,
    *UdonBehaviour.OnVideoStart*: These events should be triggered by the actual actions.

@{5de9405aea7cc52772fcc359|full_name}: 
Press event is often used for triggering uGUI button(witch defines next action) from Animation on SDK2.
For example, even VRC_Starter Kit ( https://booth.pm/ja/items/979837 ) uses Button.Press event on SDK2.
It makes SDK2->SDK3 migration easier. Without it, we need reimplement uGUI Buttons like above by UdonBehavior to make it work on SDK3.
@{5f2cc2f6c00297464bd2e59c|full_name}: Thank you for the explanation. These will continue to work in SDK2 but we are forging a new path for SDK3.

details:
Whenever someone logs in or logs out, the social menu online friends list is immediately refreshed and sorted. This results in all thumbnails jumping around, as in this video: https://www.dropbox.com/s/9zxl28qyughvgg9/2020-10-17%2009-08-59.mp4?dl=0
In particular, when expanding online friends, thumbnails can jump between the leftmost and rightmost sides of the online friends list, making it very difficult to select them.
I would suggest some combination of the following to help address this:
* When users go offline with the social menu open, make their thumbnail show the offline status (as in the favorites row) but leave the thumbnail where it is until the menu is closed
* When users on favorites lists go online, keep them in the same position (or put them at the end of the online users part of the favorites section in question) until the social menu is closed
* When users on the overall online friends list go online, put them on the rightmost end of the list (top to bottom), regardless of where they would normally be placed, and sort only when the menu is closed. Keep the current scroll position unchanged.
This will allow players to still see when friends go online or offline immediately, but will avoid moving thumbnails you might be trying to select.

details:
Not sure if this is an issue exclusive to this Open Beta but we have discovered that if you do an animation on an avatar and interrupt it before it finishes by switching into another avatar, your tracking is not restored and your avatar is either in a generic state or your lose access to hand gestures. Also tested, Reset Avatar does not fix the issue.
This works for both AV2 models and AV3 models and switching from AV2 to AV2, AV2 to AV3, AV3 to AV2 and AV3 to AV3. 
I have a YouTube video that goes through three examples of this here: https://youtu.be/yPNe3FqXTfM
Steps to reproduce: 
1. With the expression menu, start an animation.
2. Close the expression menu without canceling the animation.
3. Change into another avatar.
4. Experience results. 
I imagine this problem has to do with the fact that by interrupting the animation the avatar does not go into a RestoreTracking state to restore tracking. It is strange that the problem persists between avatars.

Edit, an additional note that I recently remembered! If you're doing an animation that you can move in, for example: one that doesn't automatically cancel when you move, and you fall off the map and hit the respawn border, your tracking in that case also tends to get messed up and odd too. I've experienced this on a previous build with some friends

details:
This is an undocumented change that is a consequence of the new nametag implementation.
Using certain characters on the old system would appear as empty spaces in VRC, allowing people to use otherwise taken names (for example IIRC Merlin, the creator of U#).
Although Tupper said this is an intended change on the Open Beta Discord discussion board, this is worth bugging anyway to both provide visibility here and record specific feedback on this undocumented change.
My view: the problem appears to stem from the link between username and the UID that VRC uses to identify people. Whilst it's probably far too much work to fix this after so many years of development, at the minimum refreshing the name change timer on release would allow people to mitigate the change.
However, I'd encourage VRC to consider releasing long-dead VRC usernames back into availability. This is good practice which has been adopted by other games with this problem over the years.
title: [1019] Nametag changes expose box characters

Really hoping they'll let us keep it the way it was.
Clear old accounts, let people get a chance at getting their name.

Going to link this also: 
https://vrchat.canny.io/feature-requests/p/remove-unique-requirement-on-display-names 
Clearing old names is a temporary solution to a problem that doesn't need to exist in the first place. It does nothing when other people are using the same name and are "active" users, and disincentivizes people from returning to the game. Giving people another roll for their name is not the point. There should be no "chance" to being called what you want.

We've replaced the box with a small centered circle in the latest build, which will still communicate an "empty" character but not be invisible or look as weird as the box. Generally, invisible non-space characters in names are not something that we want to allow.
We haven't allowed name changes to abnormal unicode for a long while, so anyone who still has these kinds of symbols in their name should already have a name change available on the website if they'd like to use something else. If not, contact VRChat Support and they'll be happy to help you out.
We are investigating alternate solutions for these naming issues, but do not have any further information to offer at this time.

This change has been mitigated, but not "completed". We do not want to encourage or allow the usage of invisible characters, but also realize the impact that this has on players that have been non-maliciously using them for a long time to have their desired names.
As such, I am marking this issue as closed instead of complete.
As noted by Aev, we are investigating some alternate solutions to this issue in particular, but don't have any more info at this time.

details:
The HTTP file upload API located at "https://vrchat.com/api/1/icon" fails to sanitize the uploaded file. 
The game will render images up to 16,000x16,000 pixels, and the API is capped to 200MB.
Additionally, files that do not match their header are not correctly identified, the only thing that determines whether an image is truly an image is the file extension.
This can cause unexpected issues when you load corrupted images, such as JPEGs that have been manipulated to uncompress very largely.
On file upload, the file should be re-rendered by the server before being stored permanently to ensure that it is properly sanitized, not too large, and compressed properly.
title: [1019] Icon API upload failure to sanitize

details:
Old 2.0 avatars with the multiple animators inventory system are now broken. This system is very widely used, and a large number of 2.0 avatars are now broken.
For reference, the inventory system works by having multiple animators that effect the avatar in different ways, most usually turning on or off gameobjects. These animators are set to off by default, so their animations do not play immediately. The avatar's main animator can turn these animators on in either emote or gesture animations using the "Behavior" keyframe (which turns on/off the first component of a gameobject). Once the emote/gesture stops playing the animator is set to off again, and this freezes the animation in its current state. So if the animator turned on a gameobject, then it will stay on until another animator turns it off.
What appears to be happening now is that on loading an avatar, all the animators on an avatar are briefly turned on even if they were off by default. This causes every inventory toggle to go off at once. Unity executes animations in order that their animators appear in the hierarcy. If the animator to set the avatar back to its default state is last in the hierarchy, everything will be fine. However, in most cases this isn't true and avatar will have a bunch of stuff toggled on/off that shouldn't be. Also, the toggling of everything on at once could potentially break some inventory systems entirely.
title: [1019] AV2 Inventory systems broken

details:
The latest beta seems to have broken stop action animation systems.
To explain what a stop action system is, consider the most simple version that triggers an audio clip on collision. This system consists of a particle system, an audio source under the particle system, and an always running animation that is setting the particle system on. The particle system is set to not loop, run only briefly, and emit only one particle that exists for a very long time. Its stop action setting is set to disable, meaning that once that one particle dies it will turn itself off. We also set the particle to die when it collides or enters a trigger. Then, on collision with an object, the particle system will turn itself and its child audio source off. The animation will immediately turn the particle system back on. This will cause the audio source to play its sound clip as it has "play on awake" checked.
As of the beta, the system still kind of works, but now something is trying to turn off the particle system every frame after its stop action has fired for the first time. This fights with the animator trying to turn it back on, and in my simple play audio on collision example it causes the audio to become garbled and repeat randomly. This does not happen in live or unity, so I am sure it is something caused by the changes made in the beta.
title: [1019] "Stop Action" animation systems broken

details: Either this, or auto-declining could be a separate toggle altogether. If streamer mode is meant to prevent you from being spammed with requests from people watching your stream, there would be no point in declining people who are in the same room as you.
title: [1065] (Streamer Mode) Have friend request auto-declining not count users in-room

comments.value:
Auto-declining friend requests is not meant to prevent viewer spam, but instead it is intended to prevent some attack cases we've seen in usage.
We could except people in the same instance as you, but that kinda opens up some surface I don't think we're OK with opening up. 
The intent was that you could still send a friend request to others when this mode is on, so its sort of a soft version of the Discord privacy options for friend requests (which might be something we eventually do). Thoughts?

Agreed. Otherwise it would just be more difficult to add people when I'm out exploring and socializing. It would still protect streamers who are in their own private instance, but wouldn't make it more difficult to add someone that I am hanging out with right now. Also, if there were two people in streamer mode, neither of them would be able to add each other without first disabling it, which wouldn't be ideal at all. Keep in mind that most people will not (or cannot due to being mute / different language) ask if they can add someone when they meet them ingame. Unless I'd be able to tell that I cannot add them right now, I also wouldn't be able to approach them and ask if they would be fine with it or not.
Also why it being a separate setting altogether would be better as to not make streamers more of a target if anyone can have it (Would also prevent friend request spam for world and avatar creators)

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: The problem is that two people in streamer mode wouldn't be able to add each other at all, as well as making it more difficult for people who are just hanging out to add people because they wouldn't know if that person is using streamer mode or not (and there are a lot of streamers in VRChat). Discord would at least notify me that I am not able to add someone, VRChat doesn't do that. And not every streamer would have an issue with friend requests from people in the room, so the lack of customizability in that regard also makes it not ideal. If two people in streamer mode would be able to add each other, it would be bypassable and defeat the original intention.
That's why I think having a separate setting for when you can and cannot be added (similar to Discord) would be the better solution. It would be separate from streamer mode (which Discord has as well) in case you do want friend requests, you would be able to prevent random friend requests from people you have never met regardless of the mode or block it out completely if you absolutely never want anyone to add you. Most importantly, Discord actually does let you know about this. I would hate trying to add someone only for that request to go into the void and me not knowing about it, so I'm not even able to ask  them if they can add me instead to see if they would be okay with it or not.

*Additionally, known streamers would receive those kinds of attacks regardless on whether or not they are streaming right now, making it even more important that it becomes a separate setting. Discord has a streamer mode and separate privacy settings for when people can add you and I think it is very useful like that to prevent random requests regardless of your mode

@{5d6ac3d319a45a329c545086|full_name}: It is a better solution, but it also is one that's outside the scope of this particular feature. We'll likely add seperate controls later, but for now, this is how Streamer mode will likely work.
If two people with streamer mode enabled want to friend each other... well, yeah, that's an (assumedly extremely rare) edge case that you kinda just have to deal with. We're fine with that being how it works for the moment.
tl;dr: yes, you have a point, but we decided to circle back around to that later when we have time

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Fair enough. If this is being addressed later on, I'm fine with it, I jus see it being a problem for me since I usually do quietly send friend requests and don't always feel comfortable approaching someone to ask. In the meantime I guess I jus, ask more often or use my avatar to communicate it. (Maybe adding the friend request symbol as an emoji could be a temporary workaround for mutes? Wouldn't really be abusable I think either)

After review, we aren't going to make a change to this behavior at this time.
These changes are intended to prevent avenues of attack. Opening up the changes a bit opens a surface we're not comfortable with in addition to complicating the feature.
If you have Streamer mode on, you can still send a friend request to others.
That being said, we definitely will consider this for future privacy features.

details:
This may seem small but if ~I~ can see it, I assume thousands of others of people will find this a bit odd or offputting.
The new avatar selection system has a change of verbage, from "change" to "wear", as in "Wear these avatars".
First, I would like to suggest, if you're interested to changing to a different word, please try "use". "Use these avatars" is very neutral sounding.
Why I feel this way is simply when I think of "wear these avatars", I feel like the connotation is the avatars are no longer 'you', you're merely 'wearing' them. Like a sweater. Since VR's goal in general is to maximize immersion and pull you into the environment, this verbage does the opposite, reminding the user that this experience isn't real, you aren't a bug or a robot or an alien, and it's that pulling "out" of the experience, the reminder that it's all smoke and mirrors, kills it a bit. 
Further, I start thinking of "wearing a body suit". Or "wearing skin", since you're essentially equipping what is akin to a "fur suit" when donning avatars. I'm sure even the furry community would prefer to "use" a furry avatar instead of "wearing" one. But mostly back to the "wearing skin" idea, bad connotations, don't like it.
title: [1065] Feeback: Usage of "Wear" Verbage

details:
(My proposed solutions are at the end)
With the new change for attempting to keep the audio and video in sync, I'm noticing a rather significant amount of hitching over time.
If I build and test with 2 clients and try to play some media (let's say it's a music video), just having them play without doing any system intensive tasks, they will become significantly out of network-sync due to audible hitching from the audio/video sync corrections.
This particular behavior was present on a previous version of my video player when it was trying to enforce a sync update just about every second.
I also noticed [pic related] happening in the logs which further cemented my assumptions about what's going on.
While this enforced AV sync keeps the video itself in-line, it breaks some syncing across clients for video players that have such features.
Please revisit the particular implementation of this AV sync enforcement.
My suggestions would be any of:
1) Make the AV resync threshold configurable through the BaseVRCVideoPlayer interface.
2) Expose a method to udon that does a one-off AV resync.
3) Allow creators and/or udon to enable/disable the forced AV resync.
4) All of the above
title: [1112] VideoPlayer Audio-Video Resync is causing significant hitching during playback

For (2 and 3): you can turn it on and off through udon. There should be a new SDK.

details:
SDK: 2021.07.08.15.57
When using any version of SendCustomEvent, an event will not appear in the dropdown list unless it actually does something.
The attached screenshots make it much clearer:
The first screenshot shows that the custom event is not attached to the SetActive node and therefore does nothing. Because of this all of the SendCustomEvent nodes have their dropdowns grayed out.
In the second screenshot the event now does something and all of the SendCustomEvent nodes have dropdowns.
While I understand that in most cases this isn't an issue (because why would you have an event node that doesn't do anything?) it could still be potentially confusing.
title: [1112][SDK][Graphs] Custom events won't appear in the dropdown if the event doesn't do anything

comments.value: Hey Igbar - this is expected. The SendCustomEvent-type nodes read the compiled program to figure out the Entry Points, and events are only included in the program if they connect to another flow. I understand that it could be confusing - hopefully examples, documentation and community knowledge ease that issue.

details:
SDK: 2021.07.08.15.57
When using SetProgramVariable to change a variable on another UdonBehavior, private variables won't appear in the dropdown. Making the variable public will make it appear in the dropdown, and if you select that variable in the dropdown and then set it to private again it will appear as "MISSING! was x" where x is the name of the variable. Leaving it like this will STILL WORK, it can functionally change private variables like it could before. Private variables just don't appear in the dropdown.
title: [1112][SDK][Graphs] SetProgramVariable won't show private variables on other UdonBehaviors

comments.value: This is as-designed, but we'll discuss internally whether it makes sense to limit these dropdowns to showing 'public' variables.
We'll make non-public variables available by adding some sort of internal prefix to variables generated by the compiler.
Fixed in next version.
Fixed in 2021.3.1 build 1113.

Uploads are direct to Amazon storage servers, so any kind of poor routing or internet issues will cause upload to be quite slow. Uploads never traverse a "VRChat-owned" network or process.
In short, uploads go as quick as they can, and we don't have any control how your upload is routed across the internet! We've made no changes to the 2019 SDK regarding uploading content (aside from marking it as "2019" content instead of "2018" content).
@{5b99d19aee038460c535199e|full_name}: "Bad Gateway" may indicate a routing problem on your ISP's end.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: already in unity 2018, uploads via the SDK are significantly slower (over 20x slower in my testing) than a single threaded upload to us-east-1 S3 using chrome. I'm not sure what your http client is doing to make it so slow, but I wouldn't dismiss this without benchmarking to see if it has gotten even worse in 2019.

I tried uploading Unity 2019 on two types of Internet lines.
Both are high-speed lines with speeds above 20M, but both are errors.

I did some further investigation. I was unable to reproduce a significant difference between upload speeds on unity 2018 and 2019. However, I was able to confirm that the SDK upload speed is _significantly_ lower than what network conditions allowed for. See https://feedback.vrchat.com/sdk-bug-reports/p/sdk-uploads-are-slow-due-to-not-filling-the-tcp-window

@{5b99d19aee038460c535199e|full_name} I will be marking this as "in progress" and link to bd_'s post.

details:
With default quality settings in open beta shadow quality for realtime directional light shadows has taken a nosedive. Shadow quality in Unity is already unacceptably bad and shadow quality just gets way worse in open beta.
Album with comparisons: https://imgur.com/a/k5EIYvv
The issue is that all quality settings that are not ultra have their shadow cascade count set at 2. This is especially an issue that the default quality level does this since it's effectively an automatic downgrade to all content and will cause complaints to world, avatar, and shadow authors over the new default. If the shadow cascades get lowered to 2, it should only be done on the Low quality setting or *maybe* medium imo.
Lowering shadow cascades has many issues for existing content. Primarily it increases light leaking significantly, where you will see light behind objects that are supposed to cast a shadow. It obviously lowers shadow quality very noticeably which turns most shadows into formless blobs. On avatars shadows were already terrible to the point that people turn off shadow casting on their avatars to avoid self shadowing. This only makes it even worse and removes what little bit of shadow resolution was left on players. Due to the lowered resolution when things move in shadows, their shadowed parts flicker much more than before as well.
title: [1118] Shadow quality regression

comments.value:
The default graphics level has been swapped to Ultra. Ultra has shadow cascades set to 4 and shadow distance set to 150, versus High which has half that value on both.
Those who have used the Open Beta will have to re-set their value to Ultra upon release.
We eventually plan on providing more granular graphical controls in the application (which will solve this issue more precisely) but do not have an ETA on this change.
To add the only difference between High and Ultra is the shadow cascades and distance settings. Ultra is equivalent to the previous VRHigh setting.

details:
In the latest Open Beta there is currently an issue where the Blend Weight count in VRLow has been set to 2 bones, compared to the old settings with 4.
With this, most avatars in the game will partially break due to bones not being able to be used for their intended purpose, especially on models that use rigging techniques such as twist bones and facial rigs.
title: [1118] VRLow Blend Weight Issues

comments.value:
This directly affects my avatar which I rigged to minimize the complexity of dynamic bone.
Looking at the antenna, the bone deformation is janked up with 2 weights. 
This is a 3 bone chain (two in the wire one in the light) to reduce the complexity of the dynamic bone calculation weighted such that with the three bones I can get a fairly smooth bend object. 
With the two influences, this effect falls apart. To make the avatar look correct, I'd need to make the rig more complex and the impact of the additional bones to the chain would counteract any theoretical performance gains from the 2 weights (which I can't imagine are much) and perform worse at all quality levels. 
People are going to rig their avatars in a way to get their desired look. If people end up having to increase the complexity of their rigs to ensure their avatars don't break on this new setting, it's going to negatively impact performance as a whole, especially on the higher settings. Based on precident, people will do that.
Low (and Quest's setting) has been swapped back up to 4 from 2.

I'm going to correct my original comment since it wasn't fully correct.
This issue is caused by duplicated or copied and pasted Animator States, Transitions, etc. being given a HideFlag value of 3, meaning it both can't be seen in the Project window OR the Inspector. Empty States created with right-click are given a HideFlag of 1, which allows them to still be inspected. 
After I went back and checked, this behavior also exists in Unity 2018.4.20f1, which means that the flags weren't being respected and probably were considered a non-issue by Unity. But as of Unity 2019.4.29f1, they are being respected, resulting in the behavior we're seeing.
I don't believe VRChat can do much about this, since this is an issue for Unity to solve, not them. That said, whatever fix Unity distributes likely won't automatically fix affected controllers, so a tool may be required to fix it. I have made a script that does exactly that which can be found here: https://github.com/Joshuarox100/Fix-Your-Animators
Appears to be a Unity bug, and unfortunately a pretty significant one. We're investigating.
