details: This issue can likely be re-produced when another user is using a taller PC avatar. Large bounds might force avatar's performance score to go down, and force Fallback mode to be activated, creating a floating Fallback.
title: [1130] PC Fallback avatars 'float'

comments.value: This is expected when your fallback is scaled and proportioned very differently from your actual avatar. Try to find an avatar close in proportions and scale to yours, or create a custom fallback. The method for scaling tries to get the viewpoints similar so you are seeing eye to eye. If the other proportions are different, this could lift or sink the fallback.

This is expected behavior. Scaling tries its best to ensure the most important points match up (viewpoint, most of all) but will fail to be completely precise in some cases.
We don't plan on improving this behavior at this time, but might circle back around to it once the Fallaback improvements have released and we've had a chance to see how they work.

details:
In a real-world camera, the zoom ratio changes in conjunction with the focal length. In the VRChat camera, focal length affects only blurriness.
I think that focal length should be computed from zoom ratio and it shouldn't be configurable separately.
title: [1137] Focal length and zoom should be interlocked

comments.value:
We're not bound by physical laws in VR, so I don't see a strict need for this - lack of interdependence allows for new photographic opportunities, great!
One could add an option to simulate this interdependence you describe for people who want to translate their real-life photography experience though.

@{5f71e194626ff47d20bfb43b|full_name}: The problem is that functions having same name behave differently between real-world and virtual-world without any reasons.
Zooming without changing the focal length is corresponding to scaling sensor size or crop center and enlarge in real-world camera. I think that the following parameter combination is the better one if you want to keep degrees of freedom. (In my opinion, focal length and F-stop are enough to the most cases.)
- Focal Length: it affects both of FoV and blurriness
- F-stop: it affects only blurriness
- Scaling: it affects only FoV
that would be much easier for those who are used to real cameras
Agree with this. Makes it unnecessarily confusing and the use case makes for more out of focus shots for no reason.

@{5f2fef67654cd449145490e4|full_name}: As a photographer for over a decade, you nailed it. I hope this is altered. It leads to confusion for pro and amateur photographers, it detracts from real world learning (skills/knowledge gained in VR can be transferred to a real DSLR) and ends up seeming kinda unprofessional to those who are pro/amateur photogs since it doesn't behave as expected.

This makes sense -- I wanted to see how it felt given that we're in VR and we aren't tied to the limitations of real life, but given that it's emulating something from real life, I agree, they should be interlocked.

details:
In live, if you're blocked by a disruptive user, they do not appear in social. However, as instance owner it's still possible to kick them by using a workaround: selecting a different user, and using the next/prev arrows on the user details page to select them and kick them.
However, in 1137, this is not possible; the user blocking you is unselectable on the here page, and by left/right arrows on other user pages. This makes instance owner/world owner kick useless - any bad actor can avoid it simply by blocking the instance owner.
Here's a video demonstrating the workaround on live, and how there is no option to kick a user blocking you on open beta: https://youtu.be/Y6Ir0XbwJZQ
Blocking instance owners is already being abused on live, and this will make it worse. Please ensure that instance and world owners can see and select all players on the here page, even if one is blocking the other.

The current implementation of the blocking system is flawed. This may be a good time to consider addressing this as the "Here" Menu would be a perfect use case for the proposed changes. 
Issue: When a user blocks you, you can't see them in social. Limited admin tools for Instance Owners can make this an issue. It can also make initiating a vote kick difficult to impossible. It can also create further abuse by allowing someone to spite block people in return for being blocked, target block instance owners and masters or target block world authors. Instance Owners are also not always around, leading to openings for abuse where the lobby doesn't have any realistic courses of action as they may be blocked by the malicious user.
Proposal: Emulate something similar to Discords blocking methodology. Blocking should not hide users from the "Here" menu. If you join an instance with someone who has you blocked, you should be able to tell by looking at the "here" menu. You shouldn't be able to interact with this person, a block should indeed mean a block, but you should be able to tell they're indeed in the lobby. This would remove spite blocking entirely as even if two people block each other, they can still see that they are in the lobby or not so makes it entirely moot. This also wouldn't negate the Instance Owner, world author, or world moderators from taking action as even if they get maliciously blocked, they can still see the person in "Here" and take action as needed. 
Gist: Everyone should be able to see blocked users and users who have them blocked via the "Here" menu but not interact with them. This would fix the main crux of the problem.

If you are helping moderate a large instance, you can't properly inform the instance/world owner of the bad actor.  As other comments have noted, this is simply further driving people to use alternative tools like log parsers, the in-game players list debug menu, and malicious client modifications to provide basic information that by all means should exist.

NaNs will be replaced to zero by applying post processing typically.
In the current implementation, the DoF simulation for previews runs before post processing and it spreads NaNs.

comments.value: I really hope that this is fixable by VRChat... I don't really want to work on like 15 Avatars again to just fix that with another shader and adjust it to the avatars and test alot around.-.

This is an issue with the shader that's being used.
Depth of Field unfortunately requires that things actually write to the Depth texture in order to properly blur them. "Unlit/Texture" does not do this.
Shaders that don't write to the depth texture properly will be blurred as if they are at an infinite distance away. There is no fix for this other than fixing the shader, or using a different shader.

comments.value:
Already left this comment on Discord, but will comment here while closing for record visibility, etc.
Anything that doesn't write to the depth texture will not be properly blurred.
Depth of Field works on the depth texture. Transparent shaders or shaders that do not have a shadowcaster pass do not write to the depth texture, so they will be blurred as if they are at the distance of the nearest thing behind the object that does write to depth. They are effectively invisible as far as the camera DoF system is concerned.
TLDR; 
This is a Unity limitation, and not something we can fix on our end.
Don't use shaders that don't write to depth.

details:
Any light grip on the opposite hand that opened the Quick Menu will unintentionally scroll any UI element after doing an open hand Gesture on the Valve Index.
How to reproduce:
- On Open Beta, with Valve Index controllers on both hands
- Make sure the Valve Index palm strap is not strapped too tight
- Make a closed fist with the Left hand and keep it in a closed fist position
- Open the Quick Menu on the Right Hand (by pressing the Quick Menu button on the Right Hand)
- Open any of the following menus of your choice:
--- Quick menu on the Right hand > Volume > point the cursor onto a slider with the Left hand
--- Quick menu on the Right hand > Select user > point the cursor onto the quick menu with the Left hand
--- Quick menu on the Right hand > Worlds (which opens the System Menu) > Point the menu on any row that is scrollable with the Left hand
- As long as the Left hand is doing a fist, the menu works by pressing the left trigger on left hand as expected
- Now, make a full open hand gesture with the Left hand by opening all fingers
- From now on, any light grip on the Left hand will cause scrolling elements to grab
- There is no force required to activate the grab with the light grip, just lightly closing the Left thumb and the middle finger around the controller should be enough to trigger the grip
Observed:
- The volume sliders of the Quick menu will move
- The Quick menu will scroll up and down
- The worlds row of the System menu will scroll laterally
Expected:
- Light grip should not cause an interaction with any scrollable element in the menu
Additional comments:
- Opening the Quick Menu on the Left hand will cause the light grip to occur on the Right hand
title: [1145] [Bug] Any light grip on the opposite hand that opened the Quick Menu will unintentionally scroll any UI element after doing an open hand Gesture on the Valve Index

details: VRChat exposes avatar OSC configuration at a well-known path. This would be very useful for building third-party applications to introspect and automatically display what an avatar can handle - however, there doesn't seem to be a good way to determine which avatar is currently being used. By exposing the user ID and avatar config file name (ie, the avatar name + avatar ID) over OSC as an OSC string, applications could automatically locate the config file for the avatar in use.
title: [1166] Please expose user ID and avatar name/ID over OSC

comments.value:
I can't mark something as partially in-progress. Please do not make reports/feedback posts that consist of more than one item!
Avatar ID will be exposed in an upcoming update upon avatar change. User ID and avatar name will not.
Additionally the full filepath of the config file in use will also be delivered.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: I think my actual intent was resolved, since I only really wanted user ID to build the config path; now that the config path is available as an OSC message, that's not needed anymore.
@{5c1475afb7ce126e9e0e3a39|full_name}: Alrighty, sounds good!

Solved via implementation of the following OSC read-outs in 1168:
`/avatar/change` is the ID of the avatar you've just changed into
`/avatar/config` is the file system path to get to the config file

details:
1. Have an avatar with something like a sets of breast bones
2. Add a Physbones script to the root of the two breast bone chains.
3. Attach a GameObject (a cube) to one of the children of the bone with the Physbone script on.
Expected:
Both bone chains transform as expected when in play mode/VRChat
Actual:
Only the bone chain without any non-bone child objects transforms.
Why this bug stinks:
There are lots of avatars that have something attached at the end of a bone chain. This is a pretty common and easy way of customizing an avatar.
A good example is a pin on someone's chest, which is what has happened in my case.
title: [1181] Non-bone GameObjects that are a child of a Physbone'd bone stop the bone transforming

comments.value: To clarify heirarchy here: Root -> Left_1 -> Left_2, Root -> Right_1 -> Right_2. If you put a GameObject parented to Left 1, the chain shuts down.
Can you try the same with an Empty instead of a Cube?
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Same effect

Okay, fixed this. It was... complicated! Implemented in the latest Open Beta. Here's what happened.
In previous betas, PhysBones ignored the additional children of parent bones that had more than one child. This was due to how virtual endpoints were generated for parent bones.† To address this, we have changed the default, and added some options for creators to decide how this is handled.
Under the Transforms section of the component, we've added the "Multi Child Type" option.
**Average** is the new default for both new PB and converted DB. It averages the position of each child bone, and uses that average as the endpoint of the parent bone. This was chosen as the default for conversions as it most closely matches DB's behavior. It isn't EXACTLY the same, however, so you will still run into cases where a manual DB -> PB conversion is required.
**First** is another new mode. It takes the position of the first child bone in the hierarchy as the endpoint for the parent bone.
**Ignore** is the previous mode, where child transforms beyond the first child are ignored.
†To be more specific, Unity doesn't have the concept of a "bone length" like Blender does. PhysBones must know the length of the bone, however, because we need to know where the child bone "hangs" from. If you simply use the head of the parent bone or one of the children as the pivot, you could end up with undesired behavior. This is why a virtual endpoint must be generated. Average should cover the majority of use cases, and it closely approximates what Dynamic Bones does. If you really want to tweak behavior and movement, you can try out the other modes.
Anyhow, this is fixed now! woooooooooooo
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Sounds like a lot of work! Thanks all for the work.

details:
This is specifically an issue with grabbing, not colliding, so far as I can tell.
Multiple people have tried using an animation to toggle "Is Animated" at runtime (i.e. disable that while grabbing, or only enable while a specific animation is happening) but it appears to make no difference at runtime.
GIF illustrating the issue courtesy of Joshuarox100.
title: [1181] Grabbing "Is Animated" Physics Bones stutters, doesn't actually move.

comments.value: Darn, seeing that even using doing this via animator does not work makes this quite hard to use.

I'm also having this issue. Tried toggling the "Is Animated" button with animations linked up to "(parameter)_IsGrabbed as well as even swapping between a set of bones, one with "Is Animated" toggled on, and the other with "Is Animated" toggled off, but the bones (which is obvious to me now) are a completely new set of bones, so they reset to the default pose, get de-grabbed and then change back to the animated "Is Animated" bones. Would love to see "Is Animated" working at runtime so people can interact with tails, ears, etc.

I think physbone might have to copy the mechanisms of dynamic bones by creating separate “particles” that are not directly attached to the bones in order to animate the bones but still perform pulling
An easy fix for this I think would be a toggle to set: Animation overrides grab or grab overrides animation.

RE: using animations to toggle "Is Animated": I just did some digging, there's a field VRCPhysBoneBase.configHasUpdated which causes the script to respond to changes in the parameters. It's set to true when modifying stuff in the inspector, and I guess it isn't set to true when an animation sets values on the script. I threw together a quick script (https://gist.github.com/kitlith/703806b980c4a613a1c70f147aec596d) to set configHasUpdated to true, and toggling "Is Animated" is handled once that field is set.
A possible fix might involve changing the config fields on VRCPhysBoneBase to properties that set configHasUpdated to true in the setter.
This may qualify as a separate bug, to be split out from this issue.
Is there any problem if IsAnimated is always true? I mean, how about setting it true even if actually animated or not.

@{5a983204a1528d415c5ced46|full_name}: That's what this post is about: having IsAnimated be true causes issues when you try to grab the bones. so it's untenable if you want to be able to grab the bones unless this behavior is changed. Meanwhile, if IsAnimated is false, animations can't move those bones around. Assuming no change, you need to be able to toggle IsAnimated in order to be able to both animate the bones sometimes, and grab them at others.
Toggling IsAnimated didn't seem to work because neither me or others who were trying it were disabling the component to reset it, and I only saw your Technical Note about that in PhysBonesTK just now. (For anyone following along, that's here: https://github.com/naqtn/PhysBonesTK/blob/main/Unity/PhysBonesTK-Dev/Assets/PhysBonesTK/Readme.md#reloading-parameters) I'm not sure requiring disabling the GameObject desirable behavior in the long run.
Nevertheless, this means that we still have a workaround in the form of disabling and re-enabling the PhysBone to refresh these parameters, including IsAnimated. I suspect this would cause janky behaviour for the idea of using a grab to toggle off IsAnimated (i.e. disabling an idle animation), but it could be made to work. 
I think I have enough information to start implementing this on my avatar.
EDIT: This workaround seems to be incompatible with the idea of animating a bone with the goal of creating a new default position for the physics bone. Toggling "Is Animated" w/ configHasUpdated does not have this issue.
My description of this is clumsy. I'll try to come back after I get some sleep, and maybe make a gif illustrating this particular case. Maybe it should be split off as a different bug. :/

@{6035ec519adad6780b906c51|full_name}: The problem with toggling the object or component off is that it would disable whatever grabbed it, causing it to re-enable the parameter.
For example, say I grabbed my ear. Then I used the Ear_IsGrabbed parameter to reset the component with Is Animated disabled. When I disable the component, it also makes it unable to be grabbed, thus resetting Ear_IsGrabbed to false, and undoing the change.
Yes, you could set a delay for reverting Is Animated back to true, but either way, people would have to grab the bone twice in quick succession to hold it.

I wonder if there will be a fix that will just *work* with IsAnimated, much like how interaction/collision works fine with it. That way you can still have animations stacked on top of it, and the deltas of the animation would still affect the movement of the bones

details:
In Dynamic Bone, the root of the branched part is also physically calculated and moved. (The root bone itself does not move, but the bones beyond it behave as if the root bone bends.)
In PhysBone, the root bone of the branched part is completely fixed.
If you prepare as many PhysBone components as the number of branches with other branches disabled, you can get the desired behavior, but it will be inconvenient, so please make the branched roots move as well.
title: [1181] Request: Enable the physics of the root bone of the branched part of PhysBone.

comments.value:
There are many branching objects that do not want themselves to move, for example, the root of a skirt or the root of a hair.
The same is true for DynamicBone, which does not update the Rotation of branching objects because it does not want them to move.
The end of the branching object changes position, but if you don't want that to move either, you can fix it by setting the Stiffness of the branching object to 1.0. (This situation also occurs at the root of the skirt and the root of the hair.)
Because of these situations, it would seem that simply allowing branching objects to move in PhysBone would break the setup now configured in DynamicBone.
I thought the best solution would be to add a simple configuration that normally does not move, but allows it to move.
This is the situation. I do not want this SkirtRoot object to rotate.

To make it easier to understand what the issue is, I made a repro video. I think possible workaround by users is inserting a GameObject between branch parent and children. The video also demonstrate this. https://twitter.com/naqtn/status/1500467312821878784

@{5f4773dac246b672791386d7|full_name}: 
In such a case, when using Dynamic Bone, I think that it has been fixed by stiffness.
If you didn't use stiffness, the bones would have moved.
I have prepared a demonstration movie.
https://twitter.com/takec_vrc/status/1500491182048428038
My suggestion is closer to the behavior of Dynamic Bone so I think the conversion will work better.
If you don't want to move it, you can fix it using immobile as before.

I think there are three possible options for the behavior of the branch part.
1. Each branch is calculated assuming that root can rotate, but root itself does not. (Fully compatible with Dynamic Bone.)
2. Calculate each branch as if root can rotate, and rotate root itself (use average or representative because the rotation of each branch may be different)
3. The branch part is completely fixed. (Current behavior of PhysBone)

This has caused headache and the workaround is what you mention or throw it in blender and add a bone before it, which probably isn't the best solution in general (definitely for the quest platform) and hope it gets fixed before release.

@{6118b1d3d8898772af0fc760|full_name}: this is a very good representation of the behaviour change we see with physbones. A lot of avatars and even a couple of bases expect the normal dynamic bones behaviour (the middle one in the video). Making it possible to get this sort of behaviour back would be beneficial, especially for the auto conversion at the moment.

I tested Phys Bone's branching behavior in build 1187.
https://twitter.com/takec_vrc/status/1514588136969748484

details:
So, I noticed that converting Dynamic Bones to Phys Bones will not really use the last bone in the chain, it will not be rotated or anything else, it will basically be ignored by Phys Bones. I know that the docs state that a chain with a single root bone and with several children (but no grandchildren) will require to manually add an endpoint. But this basically seems to apply to every Phys Bone, since if you had a chain out of 2 bones, the last bone will not be used unless you manually set an endpoint for it compared to Dynamic Bones. This basically means that every Phys Bone will always miss the last bone in the chain compared to Dynamic Bones.
I know that we can manually add endpoints to all of our bones, but why is this now always required? This does not only make it harder to manually convert to Phys Bones in your own Unity project, but will also break a lot of Avatars that can only be converted in game by the auto conversion (SDK2 Avatars and also Public Avatars that you might not have access to)
If Phys Bones would handle the end of a chain the same way as Dynamic Bones, did it would solve a lot of problems, auto conversion would work better, chains with a single root bone and with several children (but no grandchildren) would work out of the box, converting them manually in Unity would also work better since you wouldn’t need to always add an endpoint and in general it would just make it easier for everyone. Please consider changing it.
In the video I included below you can see what I mean, the whiskers will not move in the middle without manually adding an end point compared to Dynamic Bones.
https://youtu.be/oKkCS8KzNqg
In the first picture you can see how it normally should look like with both bones being used on the whiskers, this requires manually adding end points though. In the second picture you can see how it worked with the auto conversion, it completely misses the end of the bones.

details:
This is an idea for modifying (or expanding) "Limits" parameters of VRCPhysBone.

# Presentation video

I made a video to explain this request visually. See this clip: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1BcMpgJEGXrwWPllx69oF83DfqoQAoNmv/view?usp=sharing


# Previous request

Already we have another suggestion about MaxAngle: ["[1181]Separate Axis of Max Angle"]( https://vrchat.canny.io/open-beta/p/1181separate-axis-of-max-angle ). I agree that requirement and I also want such feature. But I think three pairs of angles for each axis (x,y,z) are not appropriate parameters for this issue.

The reason is:
1. The motion of each single bone doesn't have three degrees of freedom. Except for stretching, bone's tail transform can move on the surface of a sphere around its parent transform (that is the bone's head transform). In other words, it has only two degrees of freedom.
2. Two pairs of max angle defines rectangular area on the sphere surface. I guess it disturbs smooth movement of the bone at the corners. Actual velocity of bones will change quickly. (It is not differentiable in mathematics terms.)


# Anisotropic MaxAngle

So I propose an idea of "anisotropic MaxAngle with offset".

PhysBone parameter `MaxAngle` limits each bone movement within that angle. Currently, `MaxAngle` is isotropic. To make it anisotropic, let's introduce new parameter. I name it `t` for now.

This parameter changes limitation area:
- For an axis, max-angle is equal to original `MaxAngle`.
- For another orthogonal axis on the basement surface, `t` decreases "effective" max-angle as a coefficient.

If `t =1.0`:
- The basement of the cone is a circle. 
- Effective max-angle is isotropic.
- This is equal to current implementation.

If `t < 1.0`:
- The basement is like an ellipse.
- It is flattened as t decreases.
- Effective max-angle is anisotropic.

If `t = 0.0`:
- The basement is like a line segment.
- It is like `FreezeAxis = true`
- (though I'm not sure actually it will give same runtime movement.)

Notes:
- I choose the value range of `t` from zero to one for applying animation curve.
- I think `FreezeAxisAngle` can be also applied. (Though it's not "freeze".)


# Offset by angle and ratio

As previous request "[1181] Max Angle Offset slider for PhysBones" appeals, we need offset feature. (currently that post is [merged](https://vrchat.canny.io/open-beta/p/1181separate-axis-of-max-angle) )

I think specifying in polar coordinates on the basement is appropriate in this situation rather than Euler angles on the bone. Since Euler angles leads "out of limited area" problem.

An `angle` and a `ratio` specifies where the bone rest position is, viewing from limitation cone area. If we limit the value range of `ratio` as `[-1.0,+1.0]`, the rest position never goes away from the limitation area, even if you change `MaxAngle` and/or `t`.

Note: There are some choices for the value ranges,
- `angle: [0,360], ratio: [0.0,+1.0]`
- `angle: [-90,90], ratio: [-1.0,+1.0]`
- `angle: [0,360], ratio: [-1.0,+1.0]`
- etc.
I prefer symmetrical one `angle: [-180,+180], ratio: [-1.0,+1.0]`


# Use case example: bones for a skirt

## The problem and the application of anisotropic MaxAngle

Imagine PhysBones moves a skirt. If you put bones like umbrella, basically the model moves very well.

Problematic action is, you may know, moving legs up a lot. Let's consider to add `VRCPhysBoneCollider` to thighs. But, unfortunately, actual behavior would be an unexpected one. Major problems are on the root bones of each chains. They don't move up (or front) but to aside.

I guess this happens because of the pull force of PhysBone moves them to downside where the rest positions are. If we narrow `MaxAngle` to prevent from moving to aside too much, the bones simply go through thighs. If we reduce pull force, the skirt will be messy even if you're just standing.

If we can use anisotropic `MaxAngle`, we can limit side rolling but keep free area to move up (or front).


## Comparison to other methods

`FreezeAxis` can also solve this problem in same way. Though the bones don't move when you walk sideways. It's not natural enough.

Some people have used `Bound=Inside` colliders on Dynamic Bone for this issue. See https://yananann.hatenadiary.jp/entry/2018/11/17/195631  This is the reason "inside-colliders" post got many votes https://vrchat.canny.io/open-beta/p/1181-inside-colliders And now some people try to use `Plane` colliders on PhysBones same way.

Since these methods need one collider for each chain, it needs more calculation cost at runtime.

So I think anisotropic MaxAngle would be reasonable way.
title: [1184] [Request] anisotropic MaxAngle with offset

comments.value:
Supplement image:
For instance, I expect this works like this if I apply it on bones for a skirt. For the bones around waist, I squash limitation area so that bones don't roll aside. For the bones near tail of chains, bones can move any direction so that they move naturally. (I assumed I can use animation curve to change the parameter gradually.)
Although not a direct implementation of your proposal, the "polar" mode pretty closely matches the behavior you want here. Is it sufficient?

Yes, the most important part of the issue is resolved.
There remains a difference. The "polar" mode defines rectangular area, while I propose rounding area. I'm still worried about this. But I don't have problematic particular case now.
So I don't mind if you close this post. If I find a problem about that, I'll open new Canny report.

The issue with the curves has been fixed in the latest open beta. Now when it converts from stiffness to max angle, it will invert the curve. This should fix the issue where your max angle was zero.
As for the point you made about stiffness, the thing is that dynamic bones stiffness is not the same as physbones stiffness. Dynamic bone stiffness hard limits the distance that it can go away from it's original position, so max angle on physbones is the closest conversion. Physbones stiffness is a force that reduces the movement at all times, not just at that limit, so it would be very different.

details:
If multiple physbone components are using the same collider, only one of the physbones components' collision checks will be counted in stats. This will usually be the earliest one in the hierarchy.  The collision still works fine ingame, just it isn't represented in the stats. This applies both in the sdk and ingame. 
This can be easily reproduced with the Avatar Dynamics Robot Avatar scene with these steps.
1. - Open up the scene and make sure it has 36 collision checks from the hair colliding with the chest collider. 
2. - Add the chest collider to the tail, ears, or button.
3. - Check the stats again and see that it hasn't updated correctly and is still reporting having only 36 collision checks. 
4.- You can also upload the avatar and see that it's still reporting only 36 collision checks despite it having more.
Here's a video of me reproducing the issue in a blank project with the newest sdk: https://streamable.com/chskys
title: [1188] Collision checks aren't counted accurately if a collider is used by multiple physbone components

Hi!
I understand why you might want this, but **we don't plan on implementing the ability to have unlimited PhysBones on Quest.** Here's why.
PhysBones, while very performant, still hits the XR2 pretty hard given enough work to do. We try to optimize as best as possible especially for new features on Quest. This is a *brand new feature for Quest* and nothing else existed before in its place.
However, we have to be very careful. Due to the extreme prevalence of Very Poor avatars on Quest, we have far less headroom on the Quest than we expect. We already exceed Meta's recommendations for various systems by a pretty big margin, and VRChat's system-level optimizations are reaching a point of diminishing returns. 
To be extremely to-the-point: We have very significant performance problems on the Quest that we constantly push back against, and we have no interest in adding in another unlimited factor that would kill performance across the board.
As much as we'd like to let people do whatever they want whenever they want, we've previously observed that without any hard limits, average numbers tend to balloon way out of control without any way for us to reasonably fix the issue. 
That's why we've implemented the limit. If it turns out that it's extremely restrictive, we can approach it again later-- however, I do not think this is likely. 
Notably, the soft-cap on DynBones on PC has been half of the PB limit for years, and most avatar authors have adapted and dropped below that line to ensure they're performant and that everyone sees their hard work. 
Since the PhysBones limits are **double** that DB limit and Quest has never had a system like this before, I expect Quest avatar authors to adapt extremely quickly, and with very little loss of fidelity.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Doesn't have to be unlimited.. 
What about having the checkbox raising the limit? Would that be a good compromise?

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Appreciate the quick reply. You're right, the Physbones limits are good enough and I believe adaptation and optimization is better than just throwing more power and lower fps at the problem.
As Long as VRC has to support Quest 1, the Physbone limit will stay like that

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Use a configurable limit identical to the dynamic bone limiter, and allow safety settings for enabling and disabling PB components separately from interactions/contacts, perhaps even a limit that is adjustable for each user rank. Now you can have friends and trusted users have a more reasonable limit, and at the same time a fraction of a full lobby will have these components enabled rather than everyone. Please reconsider such a situation.

Welp. This is what happens with EAC games. Pleased to have you. Now then, for a bandaid solution and explanation.
From what I've heard, lightingservice.exe has some sort of security issue, hence why EAC blocked it. It's infuriating. This problem is not unique to VRChat, but literally every game with EAC.
The solution? Create a .bat script and put it on your desktop, that when launched will automatically kill the lightingservice.exe task.
Step 1: Open notepad in windows. Yes. Stock notepad.
Step 2: type in "taskkill /IM lightingservice.exe /F" without quotes.
Step 3: Save it, BUT change the "Save as type" from "Text Documents" to "All Files". Then remove ".txt" from the end of the file name, and replace it with ".bat" instead. You may name it whatever you want. That doesn't matter.
Now you have a batch script that when launched, will automatically kill LightingService. (You might have to right click and run as administrator since /F forces it to close.)
You can put this file anywhere. On your desktop for easy access, in a folder. Anywhere you like.
This, while not a permanent solution, at least saves you the effort of constantly having to open task manager to kill that task yourself EVERY TIME you launch any game with EAC.
Unfortunately, I haven't found a way to make this automated more than this. But neither am I smart.
So before running any game with EAC, use that script, and then launch the game. Since lightingservice launches on boot, you have to do this every time you start up your pc to play a game with EAC, VRChat included.
Note that this does not remove the program outright. Which I doubt you'd want anyway. It just automates its shutdown.
It might make your fancy rgb lights return to defaults, since lightingservice is not running to control it.
Hope that helps. Now, let's hope Asus updates their software... one day.

@{60285ca04963ba22994f485b|full_name}: Why can't you solve everything by simply updating VRChat to not have EAC?

@{60285ca04963ba22994f485b|full_name}: This appears to /actually be/ an OSC application, though. From a purely scholarly standpoint - Is this response based on assumption, because it was picked up by EAC, or was it confirmed to be accessing via other means? If the latter, how was this confirmed?

@{5c2b681d48d73c375c04bb9f|full_name}: Devil's advocate here, but have you tried to run the application after the EAC window goes away? I've another OSC application that I use that only seems to properly cooperate with the client if launched after that point.

@{6019bf5a7ae30b2338107fb4|full_name}: I'm sure that this is a legitimate OSC application. However, in addition to communicating with VRChat through OSC, it appears to also be using a function to check if VRChat is running. That function is not using OSC and while it is not "modding" the client in a way that would be against terms of service, it is still poking at VRChat in a way that triggers EAC. 
This is something that we can bring up with Epic to see if they can allow. Alternatively, VRChat could implement some other method of informing applications that is running. We will have to investigate the options. In the meantime, applications should be changed to simply not worry about whether or not VRChat is running.

@{60285ca04963ba22994f485b|full_name}: I suppose it depends on /how/ they're going about it exactly. I would assume that waiting on OSC to establish a connection would not violate ToS, but could still be used to make the same prompt. Likewise, there are methods to query the system directly rather than the client. Though those don't need to create an application hook to VRChat or its components, what you say seems to raise a gray area that needs to be clarified.

@{6019bf5a7ae30b2338107fb4|full_name}: There are many different ways to tell if an application is open using various windows APIs. I do not know which ones trigger EAC and which ones do not. Unfortunately people will just have to experiment with that and see what works. However, none of those methods use OSC unless you choose to listen to port 9001, and only one application can do that at once so it is not ideal.
We understand that this is not a perfect solution as it is very handy to know when VRChat is running. There are several options that would solve this that we have already considered in the past, such as OSCQuery, but this issue will raise the priority of implementing those options.

@{5ca74f3fb98a820b3ffec9cf|full_name}: this mirror indeed dont work.

Most likely this is because VRChat has unintentionally moved them to a different sorting layer other than the "Player" layer, which is the collision layer in Unity that refers to both the Local and Remote user in-game.
This sorting layer is largely important (as a world creator myself) because Mirrors need the "Player" layer in order to render the players in the world in the first place. Most mirrors in worlds show ALL layers, while some many others use the "Default", "Player", “Environment”, and "MirrorReflection" layers ONLY, which in a nutshell, are the only 4 layers needed for a High Quality Mirror.
So if the calibration dots are in for say "UiMenu" layer instead, they will NEVER show in such mirrors because that layer was purposely culled by the world's creator.
Source: current version of the World SDK 3.0

details:
There I was: a humble yet-innocent VRChat user, idly deciding to see how the tooltips (of which I almost always keep disabled) fared against the plethora of new options in the long-fabled UI2.0 main menu.
All was relatively well in the kingdom, when to my utmost horror... I noticed... **a flaw.**
A flaw so grave- in fact- that it felt as if the very earth beneath me was crumbling apart, and I immediately fell onto the ground in a fit of vertiginous despair.
The tooltip for the MSAA option in Advanced Graphics Settings... suggests that aliasing would be *increased* with a subsequent heightening of sample counts, rather than *decreased*, as the function is *intended* to achieve by design.
My horror didn't stop there, for I quickly noticed that **the fundamental NATURE of the setting itself should be called into question**, as it was actually an option for Multisample ALIASING all along!!! Not an "anti-" in sight!!!!
What is this option? What is the point of this option?! Is the fact that it's hidden at the bottom of the Performance menu under "Advanced Graphics Settings" VRChat's attempt at hiding THE TRUTH??!?!? HAVE THE DEVELOPERS BEEN SCHEMING TO MAKE US ALL SUBTLY ACCEPT ALIASING MORE AND MORE IN OUR LIVES; BEING PAID OFF BY MAJOR HEADSET MANUFACTURERS SO THAT THEY NO LONGER NEED TO INNOVATE PUSHING HIGHER PIXEL DENSITIES FOR FUTURE HARDWARE????????!?!?????????????!?!?!?!??!?!?!??? 
WHAT WILL *THEY* ADD ALIASING TO NEXT.... OUR VERY SOULS??????????????????????????????????????????????????????
(I also found the tooltip for the UI > Visuals > Background Designs dropdown to be the same as the Verbose Mode Settings dropdown; duplicated prefab? lol)
title: [1241] Anti-aliasing option text AND tooltip are completely and UTTERLY incorrect, and call into question the very nature of their (and our) existence.

details:
On Build 1284, local animator parameters seem to be represented as Floats in animators, and in the avatar debug menu - see first attached image. Bool parameters that are unsynced (only used in an Animator, not listed in synced parameters) are correctly shown (and used) as Bool on Live (1282), but are represented (and used) as Float on Beta (1284).

This regression breaks existing AV3 systems that rely on local bools (or ints) to transition between states, which impacts a fair number of avatars and prefabs.

As an example, I use parameter drivers to drive local bools for toggling parts of my avatar's body, to prevent clipping through clothes. This system works on Live (1282), but breaks on Beta (1284) - see second attached image, with skin peeking through hoodie due to the transitions not firing. Other, more complex systems (such as custom locomotion controllers) would be more negatively affected.

details:
- PhysBones have been adjusted to use and maintain the initial hand-to-bone offset** as your "grab position" instead of a fixed relative position per bone. This means that grabbed PhysBones won't move or "snap" when you initially grab. They will only move when you move the grabbing hand.

Please allow creators to disable this functionality on a per physbone basis. While it is great for hair or other natural uses of physbones, some technical uses of physbones are negatively impacted by this change. For example, some systems use physbones to snap objects to you or other peoples hands adding interactivity to props. Avatars that use physbones to measure how far a object is pulled (one example would be like a rip cord on a chainsaw prop, or a handle on a transforming scythe) will no longer be accurate and will no longer place the hand in a good position. 

Please consider giving us this option.
title: [1284] Physbone snap to hand option

Private avatar which is used in the video is 'avtr_3d4375f5-51d1-4540-9e87-fdcde52ed026'. I'm preparing public one.

@{5e877e5e60de627e6ba7946a|full_name}: I've uploaded small avatar to test this behavior. this avatar is based on 2a7s and white plate on left arm instead of wahuku because both cloth and avatar in the video cannot make public. avtr_c92d2517-c4b6-47ba-b5b4-ff5300cb7775

This bug is the result of another bug fix. However, this is in itself an undocumented, unintended use case and only worked before due to a quirk in execution order.

To break the issue down:

- Avatar author makes a single GameObject with both a Constraint and PhysBone component attached to it.

- Frame begins.

- The Physbones solve themselves. Gravity is enabled, so it moves downwards towards gravity.

- The Constraints solve themselves. This moves the root of the chain which affects all of the bones.

- Frame is rendered.

*We will not be fixing this bug.* Fixing this bug would require changing the execution order of either Constraints or PhysBones, which would break a **very** large number of other avatars.

Another fix would be for us to provide a replacement Constraint system, but that is out of scope. We want to do this eventually, as native Unity Constraints have many problems, but we cannot do it now.

For now, please use this workaround:

Move the Constraint component "up" to the parent GameObject. Leave the PhysBone component on the original GameObject. This will fix the issue.

details:
# Issue: 

With Phys Bones Version 1.1 Gravity was changed to only apply at resting position according to the change log. This works fine in most scenarios, but when you don't have any pull on a Phys Bone, Gravity just does nothing. This results in the bone just being static at what ever position your movement or someone grabbing it moved it to.

**Reproduction Steps:**

1. Create a bone chain in Unity made out of 3 elements.  

2. Apply the Phys Bone settings as shown in the Attachments (you can ignore the Max Angle Curve)  

If you do this you will notice that even if you move the Phys Bone away from their origin by either spinning it around or by grabbing it, Gravity will not have an affect on it and it will not be pulled down.

# Expected Behavior:

If there is no Pull to bring a bone back into it's resting position (so Pull being at 0), Gravity should just always be applied.

Other than that I have to say that I don't think changing the way Gravity behaves in general is a good decision. It made sense with how it worked before (it would always be applied as a force no matter what) since... well... that's how gravity works. Because if something has pull on it, I would expect gravity to try and fight against that pull. (depending on the orientation obviously)

I do think that the change Stiffness received makes though as the new behavior is closer to (at least in my opinion) how you expect it to work.

# Attachments:

Here is a video showcasing the issue:

https://files.catbox.moe/19uvty.mp4

Here is a picture of the used Phys Bone settings:
title: [1301] Phys Bone 1.1 Gravity does not work at all with 0 Pull

comments.value:
@{5fca5df4d58780532024a52b|full_name} This is expected behaviour, as gravity is no longer a force.  We have some dev notes coming out here soon that will give a more detailed explanation.  Here is a snippet from that info.

"Previously: Gravity acted as a force which competed with Pull.  To get a specific look you needed to balance the ratio of these two values.

Now: Gravity acts directly as that ratio of how much gravity deforms the rest position of your bones.  A value of one means your bones will always fall straight down, a value of 0.5 means it will hover half way between the rest position and the world down vector.

In practice we have found this to be easier to tweak the look you are going for.

Since gravity is no longer a force, Pull is the only force that dictates how fast the bones will fall into their new rest position.  Previously many things that pointed straight down would look like (Pull: 0 Gravity: 0.3).  Now that would need to be configured like (Pull: 0.3 Gravity: 1.0)."
@{5e877e5e60de627e6ba7946a|full_name}: Thanks for the detailed explanation. This makes more sense to me now. ^^
closing as this is expected behaviour per above comment

details:
This issue involves a base model with a built-in collar that is "fused" and made invisible by setting the scale to 0,0,0. To make the collar visible again, an animation is played to change the scale back to 1,1,1. The collar has a root part that represents the actual collar, and physbone components that enable it to dangle around the neck/chest. In the beta version, when the collar is scaled from 0,0,0 to 1,1,1, the physbone components ("Tag" part) disappear and are nowhere to be seen on the model, causing unexpected behavior.

To replicate this issue, follow these steps:

1. Create a base model with a Collar and a root part.

2. Add physbone components to the collar for movement.

3. Set the scale of the collar to 0,0,0 to make it invisible.

4. Play an animation to change the scale back to 1,1,1 to enable the Collar.

5. Observe that the "Tag" part of the collar with physbones is now missing and not visible on the model after upload.
title: [1301] Scaling Physbones "hides" objects.

If creators care enough about the game balance of their world to not want this, then they care enough to spend 5 minutes going to the website to change it.

I would not even go for the "default off for worlds tagged game" there are way too many worlds that have the tag game just because they have something like beer pong somewhere but are just a chill world overall

We already have the discussion about disabling scaling limits in Friends+ instances and more private.

Maybe this would be a compromise here as well: if world authors didn't set the option - assume it to be disabled - as long as people are in public instances. details:
It would be nice if a float that matched the current avatar scale was exposed to avatar animators. Being able to adjust things on the fly based on the current scale would be wonderful.

EG: Head proportion. When I make a taller version of my avatar I usually bump the head scale down to 90% to make it feel proportional. 

Some constraints with offsets will also break when scaled and this could be alleviated by letting us manual adjustment them based on the current scale.
title: [1311] Avatar Scale Parameter

comments.value:
Additional suggestion: Consider (additionally) providing the inverse scale as an animator parameter. I.e. if the multiplicative scale is 1.1, inverse scale would be 1/1.1, or 0.9090 repeating.

This is targeted specifically at the scale invariance usecase. While I know of a way to perform division/reciprocation using blendtrees (making use of the normalize blend weights option, making sure that weights other than the divisor are canceled out with an equal negative weight), it breaks if the divisor is less than 1 (aka, the avatar is scaled smaller than default).

There is a way to make the division work with an arbitrarily small divisor, but it comes at a potential performance risk. (if you want to support divisors that are at least 1/10, you need to list 10 copies of that divisor.) So, it seems like it would be better if VRChat did this, and provided it as an animator parameter for us.

Note that head proportion changes will require further adjustment of the eye height to work properly. That said, a parameter is important for other reasons (eg - adjusting face camera culling parameters).
Here's an example of how a face camera can break down as a result of culling parameters not being adjusted for the avatar scale.
This seems like an edge case until you start thinking about the uses. There are a lot of technical reasons to add this but also some really fun creative functions.

Would this be a read-only parameter or a read-and-write parameter?

The reason I ask is that read-only is easy. Read-and-write is interesting, but it complicates the feature request and requires further consideration and time.
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Read-only would be a good start
Yeah, read only makes sense to start. Read/write would be cool, especially with OSC integration, but that's bonus. Read-only at least keeps parity with what already exists.
@{5fa08ddb2644fb4c5a3dfe75|full_name} @{6283dd169e8db10b6d6f35cb|full_name}: Got it. That's a way easier sell. Thanks!

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Read only would be nice to be able to manually fix things so that niche scaling issues could be addressed by the avatar creator. 

Read-write would be great to be able to give avatar creators more options with AV3.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Ideally read/write, as that would allow avatar creators to do scaling based animations, i.e. replicating Pokemon Gigantamaxing, something I had seen pulled off prior to this beta.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Id say read only is a good start, but most creators would really prefer to be able to write to it to. I've done avatars that rely on scaling the avatr when the user wants, for example an alice in the wonderland avatar that when you eat or drink something you shrink or get bigger, i did it using something similar to gogo loco's scaling, but now thats broken, and the parameter not being a write parameter i cant even fix that feature at all. Please make it write too

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: I personally would love to have it be read and write, could make for some interesting interactions.

Personally would use it as a donation incentive or trying to beat a game world while slowly losing height as a challenge.

I also want a bool parameter for whether the avatar scaling radial menu is open.

EG: When the cloth component is on, it is not affected by avatar scaling, so I want to turn it off during settings.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Read/write would definitely be the hoped goal for the future, or at least being able to use the scaling value to automatically drive a custom animation. Being able to have the scale drive a mesh swap and some particles would be amazing for things like a werewolf transforming avatar or like Bruce Banner to Hulk, etc.
@{5c1475afb7ce126e9e0e3a39|full_name}: Is this the native face camera? If so, please submit a seperate Canny!
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: for my purposes read only is fine. Read write would be interesting too, but more of a niche gimmick imo
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: nope, this is a custom one I use because I don’t like the layers and culling distance of the native one
GoGoLoco is a thing you know. Just use that. It's WAY less limited than ANYTHING that VRChat will force into the world
@{6222e4f65a32390981ca1962|full_name}: I'd personally like to solve a game world while slowly GAINING height ^^
@{62a7cc4b5bb57d0bb240b0cb|full_name}: Worlds can now be built with that explicitly in mind, through world authorative scaling. ^-^

@{62a7cc4b5bb57d0bb240b0cb|full_name}: You might have missed the memo that VRChat is planning on patching all bugs that are used for avatar scaling going forward, now that they have a solution that they're planning to support. (They likely held off on patching the bugs until they had a solution they were willing to support.)

@{6035ec519adad6780b906c51|full_name}: I don't want any authorization to do stuff! It's my avatar! I can do whatever the heck I want to do with it, WHERE EVER I want! World creators shouldn't get to decide what I do with my avatar! I don't care how it breaks the world, it's MY avatar! Not theirs!
@{6035ec519adad6780b906c51|full_name}: What bugs? I don't know of any size changing bugs. Everything is just fine for me :D

@{62a7cc4b5bb57d0bb240b0cb|full_name}: The GoGoLoco route adds extra complication and a performance toll I don't care for. Each individual animator layer, running or not, has a performance toll. VRC adding adding a scale param fixes any issue  I have with their scale system. (or allows me to fix my own issues like constraint offsets) The most recent beta has scale parameters and it's wonderful.

@{62a7cc4b5bb57d0bb240b0cb|full_name}: The GoGoLoco scaler works *because* of a bug. which is why it's apparently in the Go "Broke" variant, because the expectation was that it was going to be broken at some point, and that has always been the communication from VRChat -- this is going to break eventually, and they consider the fact that it isn't currently broken in the open beta a bug.

@{62a7cc4b5bb57d0bb240b0cb|full_name}: Then this is the incorrect place to make that complaint, because this canny post is not about whether worlds get control and when, it's about increasing visibility of the current scale of the avatar, so that avatar authors can make decisions based on the current scale.

comments.value: How does avatar scaler effect a particle system with different Scaling Modes?
This is a particle option within Unity, not a VRChat issue. Setting your particle setting "scaling mode" option from "local" to "hierarchy" should fix this.

Won't be fixed.

This is a particle option within Unity, not a VRChat issue. If you set your particle setting "scaling mode" option from "local" to "hierarchy", that should fix this. 

Within Unity, this is an intentional choice. Setting scaling mode to "local" is the default setting. When set, it completely ignores all the parent's scales, and only uses the local transform. 

Swapping it to global means that we are forcibly changing the scaling mode of everything to "hierarchy", which would break a large number of systems.

Users should update their particle systems to use "hierarchy" to fix this issue.
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Thanks for the heads-up! Hopefully this can be noted on docs.vrchat.com, if it isn't already. <3

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: this solves one issue in regards to the scaling and particles but not completely because while setting the scaling mode from local to hierarchy should fix some issues, other issues such as physics (gravity, limit velocity, noise, etc.) do not scale with your model. It may be worth revisiting this issue as many do not have the luxury of going back and using the scale factor parameter to fix their particle's physics.

details:
# Issue:

When using a relatively tall Avatar that is above the max 5m, it wont really work with the new Avatar Scale system.

The Avatar works fine for the most part, but once you use the scale system you are going to be limited to the 5max until you reset your Avatar. 

# Expected Behavior / Suggesion:  

I'm honestly not sure on what the best behavior would be here, but I have 3 ideas:  

1. Limit the height to 5m once they load into the Avatar.

- This would result in the limiting system actually doing it's job  

- It would kinda break / limit people with tall Avatars though

2. Set the max height to the Avatars default height if it's above the 5m limit

- people would still be able to have big Avatars this way  

-  it would kinda defeat the point of a 5m max system

3. Make the system scale factor instead of view height based  

- people could always scale up / down their Avatar no matter who tall it was originally  

- it would be really hard to implement height limits this way
title: [1311] Avatar Scaling does not work correctly with Avatars which are bigger than 5m

comments.value:
Novelty avatars such as giant Kaiju or spaceship sized avatars certainly have a place on VRC so supporting these avatars should still happen.

I feel if a world has an Udon set height limit then it should rescale the avatars, but if not, then setting the size wheel to 100% should snap the avatar back to its original size.

After further consideration I think the current behaviour is fine? (for the most part) It allows you to use the scaling, but only between the 5m max and 0.2m min height. But you can technically also be in your original bigger height.

My only grip really is that it's kinda hard / annoying to get back to your original height. As you currently need to either reset the entire Avatar or go through the Main Menu for it. 

To improve this maybe consider making the 5m max a snapping point and once they are at it, they get set to original height instead of the 5m limit? Or adding a separate button to reset the Avatar Height if your Avatar is above the 5m or below the 2m limit.

In discussion on the discord general consensus is that users want Avatar Scaling Enabled by default. The announcement states that the default for worlds is for Scaling to be disabled.

As a compromise I think it'd be a good idea to have Scaling ON by default for NEW WORLDS going forward as a qol improvement, even if just in the upload UI for the world in unity, while grandfathering OLD WORLDS into the system with Scaling turned OFF to make sure those worlds retain their previous behavior as per the 'Why is Scaling off by default?' question in the FAQ for the beta post. I really appreciated the addition of extra accessibility emojis as someone who rarely speaks aloud in VRChat, but I would REALLY appreciate if the emoji wheels were re-organized to make selecting "useful" emojis easier.

Currently, the "yes," "no," "what?," "stop," and "go" emotes (along with a couple others) that are actually very useful are scattered across pages 1 and 4 of the emoji categories. This could also be done by nesting a second accessibility page into the accessibility section instead of replacing 'page 4' with an 'accessibility 2,' for example.

I've attached some mockups of what I had in mind for this new organization so I can better explain my reasoning. (To be clear, I've only done this to better prove my point. I understand that the team might organize these slightly differently in practice.)

If you're wondering where the purple arrow came from, it's because this is from another suggestion I made for a "me"/"here" emoji on this post: https://feedback.vrchat.com/open-beta/p/1311-add-a-melook-at-me-emoji-to-the-accessibility-category-in-the-form-of-a-rev

# Issue:

I've made a script that enforces the max / min height if someone joins with / switches to an Avatar that is bigger / smaller than what is allowed. I still want people to be able to change their height inside that limited range though.

Doing this is currently impossible however, as enabling manual scaling puts the player back at their original / set height even if it's outside of the bounds I've set in my world.

# Expected Behavior:  

Enabling Manual Scaling through Udon should not set the player back to their original / manually set height, especially not if their original / manually set height is above / below the set limits.  

With this current behavior it's impossible to create a system that enforces the min / max height while also still allowing people to change their height in a given range. Which is what I think most people would want to do for game worlds.

details:
When a scale constraint is attached to a bone in an avatar, and you scale the avatar in-game, the scale factor is applied double to the bone in question. That is, if I set a scale constraint pointing to a transform whose scale is always 1,1,1, then doubling the scale of my avatar will quadruple the world scale of the target of the scale constraint.

This effect occurs only in client; scaling the root of the avatar in the unity editor does not have this effect, so something strange seems to be happening in the VRChat client here.

I've uploaded an avatar which reproduces this issue here: avtr_4fea6b0c-ed50-467c-97d1-bdfa7ec03169

The expected behavior is that both spheres should have the same size; one has no constraints on it, the other is linked by a scale constraint to an object under the avatar root which always has 0.1 scale.

This bug impacts the popular "marshmallow PB" booth asset, resulting in what could perhaps be charitably referred to as "breast explosions".
title: [1314] Scale Constraints double the scaling effect in game

In the Main Menu Search Tab we now have two "suggested" Searches, the Recommended Searches and the Quick World Searches. Both of these come with their own separate buttons for suggestions.

The buttons for the Recommended and Quick World Searches should have the same color palette, just like every other button in the menu.

This should be the case for two reasons:

This is a known Unity engine bug which affects some VR headsets, particularly Pimax and WMR.  The same bug affects several games.  As far as I know, Unity has never fixed it, and each game has had to apply what seems to be a fairly simple workaround to avoid the bug.  It has to do with a mode selection within Unity, and there's another mode which essentially works similarly but does not experience the bug.

This bug is only occurring in the VRChat Open Beta.  It is not occurring in the normal release version.

Here's a Pimax forum post discussing the issue across several games:  https://community.openmr.com/t/unity-2020-bug-inaccurate-rotation-when-looking-around-other-incompatibilities/33934/44

Here's the Unity bug that causes this discussed on the Unity forums.  This includes descriptions of how to workaround the bug:  https://forum.unity.com/threads/turning-issue-with-pimax-and-some-wmr-headsets.1205707/

This workaround needs to be implemented by the VRChat devs in order to resolve this issue.  The bug has already been present in Unity for years, and Unity can't be bothered to fix it, so don't hold your breath on that.

@{5f42e5a54014a60529c7931e|full_name}: This doesn't appear to be a Pimax bug.  The same issue affects WMR headsets, too.  It's a known Unity engine bug which has been reported for years.  It keeps appearing in multiple games, and the developers for each of those games have had to individually apply a workaround to resolve it.

It keeps rearing its ugly head over and over again in new game releases because Pimax and WMR have relatively little market share, and devs generally aren't testing against them.  Otherwise they'd find and resolve the issue early before the public ever saw it.  Also probably why Unity can't be bothered to fix it.

- Reduced friction in testing builds

details:
1: In the open beta, load into a world that contains a DXT1 texture with a texture resolution that isn't a power of 4 (see the example world)

2: The game will crash.

This seems to be a bug in the editor of Unity 2019.4.31f1 allowing you to create invalid DXT1 textures, though I haven't checked if this is fixed in 2022.3.5f1's editor.

If you take a 4x4 texture and set its texture shape to Cube, its resolution will be halved to 2x2 - and since DXT1 requires texture resolutions in powers of 4, this becomes an invalid texture.

Ordinarily, Unity will prevent you from making a DXT1 texture with a resolution that isn't a power of 4, but the Cube texture shape seems to bypass this check.

On the live version of VRChat, the game will throw an error similar to the following into the output log, without crashing:

`Texture 'sky_Texture' has dimensions 2 x 2 which is not supported for format 'RGB Compressed DXT1|BC1' (requires multiple-of-four dimensions). Falling back to 'RGBA 32 bit'.`

On the open beta, that error will also be thrown, but the game will also crash.

Here's an example world: https://vrch.at/8wp08x26

This issue seems to only be present in worlds from my testing; *avatars* with invalid DXT1 textures throw the above error, but don't crash the game.
title: [1342] Non-power-of-4 DXT1 cube textures crash the game

details:
In previous SDK, we can workaround avatar validation by calling `VRC_SdkBuilder.ExportAndUploadAvatarBlueprint` which was marked `[PublicAPI]`.

I really need to call that to avoid false-positive Avatar Validation Errors. There are many false positive avatar validations errors:

- For Avatar Validation, EditorOnly can be skipped. Materials with pc shaders under EditorOnly may cause false-positive avatar validation errors.

- When we reduce some PhysBones with IVRCSDKPreprocessAvatarCallbacks, quest PhysBone hard limit error is false-positive.

- When we replace shaders with IVRCSDKPreprocessAvatarCallbacks, PC Shader errors are false-positive. 

Of cource, I think it's not good to skip validation, but pre-build validation can cause tons of false-positive.

So, for Control Panel, I think it's OK to disallowing clicking "Build and Publish" button if there are Avatar Validation errors.

However, for calling `Build` or `BuildAndUpload` by tools, please defer Avatar Validation after `IVRCSDKPreprocessAvatarCallbacks`.

See Also: 

- [Canny about pre-building performance rank with Preprocess Callbacks](https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/sdk-please-provide-hook-on-calculating-pre-building-avatar-performance-rank)

- [Canny about post ProcessCallback Performance Ranks on build](https://feedback.vrchat.com/sdk-bug-reports/p/theres-no-way-to-know-actual-post-preprocesscallback-avatar-performance-rank)
title: [Beta SDK 3.3.0] Please Validate hard limits after processing Preprocess Callbacks in `BuildAndUpload`.

details:

---

(update2:) After further investigation, this is actually two separate issues. The information below update1 and the new clip demonstrate SyncPulse's Pimax issue, which has now been resolved for both Pimax and WMR.

This post is for the issue listed above, where it seems like the game flickers between the current and previous orientation as you rotate, but only at seemingly random times for similarly random durations.

It feels like if reprojection was kind of broken, but it happens even while the framerate is locked at 90. This flicker only happens in VRChat's view, the SteamVR dashboard and WMR start menu do not flicker on rotation.

This still occurs up to the current beta [Build 1381], though at this point I may have built up a tolerance to it so I don't notice as much.

---

(update1:) It seems they occur at specific angles, see the (New clip) video at the bottom for a better clip.

Every now and then the viewpoint flicks to an incorrect orientation for a few frames and back again. The issue does not occur on Live's Unity 2019.

Unsure if it can be fixed on VRChat's end, as it also occurs in Zenith MMO (Unity 2021), meaning it may be an issue across newer Unity releases such as the one this Open Beta is testing (Unity 2022).

I hope people don't actually upload any new SDK2 avatar content anymore, but existing content is out there and is using said system.

This is the most popular tool, which generated those toggle systems: https://github.com/Xiexe/VRCInventorySystem-DEPREACTED---USE-AVATARS-3.0-

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the VRChat Open beta on Unity 2022 in VR

2. Switch to an SDK2 Avatar with toggles (here is one of mine, which exhibits the issue: `avtr_fc8e07ab-b0e1-4cfa-ade2-2c975267e0aa`, its lightsaber and smartphone toggles work on live, but are broken on beta in VR)

3. Try to use said toggles (other people in the lobby should be able to see the issue too, provided they are on the beta and in VR)

## Possible Solutions

1. Find why those systems are breaking and fix the issue in the client

2. Block SDK2 uploads (optional) and server side migrate SDK2 content and the toggle systems to SDK3, that would mean somehow loading the old assetbundles, altering them and repacking them. I am not sure unity has some way to do that properly, it may require cursed code to do.

3. ~~Ignore the problem and pretend SDK2 content doesn't exist~~

From what was stated in the dev updates about this feature, this is sort of 'intended' behaviour.

The reason for this being that you can only have one world "guaranteed preloaded" at a time. Previously preloaded worlds are then unmarked as preloaded because they can get overwritten by other things in the cache and aren't "protected" from what I understand.

That being said, I still agree that this should change though. I think it's kind of a given that you can't expect all of your preloads to last forever. The most recent preload can still just be the "guaranteed one" while the others remain marked as preloaded. I feel like unmarking them when they're not actually gone from the cache is kind of confusing behaviour for both new and veteran players.

I have commented on Valve's VRChat issue with full details including VRChat and Proton logs.  I'm reporting it here as well since it is specific to the Open Beta:

https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton/issues/1199#issuecomment-1732524122

2023-10-4 update: Steam does not enable h264 decoding by default!  You'll need to manually enable this if the video portion of the audiovisual stream does not show.

2023-10-19 update: With VRChat 2023.3.3p1 stable release, this crash now impacts VRChat stable, and it crashes on Proton 8.x, too!  I've posted a new comment to Valve's VRChat issue with all the test results and debug logs:

https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton/issues/1199#issuecomment-1770336669

2023-10-20 update: VRChat now disables AVPro by default on Linux.  You can pass "--enable-avpro-in-proton" to the Steam launch properties to continue testing.

Steps:

1.  Set up SteamVR on Linux (tested with Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, HTC Vive, AMD RX 5600 XT)

2.  Make sure h264 video codec is unlocked in Steam, e.g. by running "steam steam://unlockh264"

3.  Install VRChat

4.  Configure VRChat properties to force "Proton Experimental" as the compatibility tool (to work around audio blasting at 100%, a recent Proton 8.0 stable regression)

5.  Load the Show Talents game world in VR: https://vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_20f170b0-57b4-4673-a8a7-329ebc07e047

6.  Walk towards stage, wait for video to load

7. If on desktop, do something to cause VRChat audio/video playback to stutter (e.g. taking a 4K photo with the camera, loading the CPU, toggling on personal mirror, switching avatars)

8.  Crash

Please see the linked Valve issue tracker for the full test matrix - VRChat open beta crashes crashes on VR and desktop (with some effort); VRChat stable works in both situations.

I realize this issue may be in Valve's court; this feedback post can be closed if so.

Last retested: 2023-10-19

 * VRChat QM build: 1370

 * Proton Experimental: 1697215757 experimental-8.0-20231011b
title: [1370] Open Beta: AVPro players crash on Linux with Proton Experimental

comments.value:
It turns out I missed two important bits of information, so I've edited my main feedback post as well as my GitHub comment on Proton (linked in that feedback post):

#1 - Fresh Steam installations don't include the h264 video codec unlocked by default.  You have to run "steam steam://unlockh264" or such then restart Steam to enable the visual part of video playback in VRChat.

After including that step, I can recreate this crash in VRChat Desktop mode on both my normal computer and a lower-powered system as well.

#2 - Any substantial AVPro audio/video desync (e.g. VRChat stuttering) results in the Desktop mode crash on VRChat Open Beta with Proton Experimental, it doesn't need to be 100% CPU load.

On my normal computer, I may need to load all CPU cores to 100% and toggle on the personal mirror or switch avatars until VRChat media playback stutters enough to trigger the crash.

On a lower power system, I just had to toggle on personal mirror for the first time with the media playing, and that stutter was enough to trigger the crash.  And I was wearing the default Robot avatar, nothing heavy.

(NOTE₁: In my limited testing, the Unity media player - e.g. as in the "iY MMD World" - has recovered from stuttering without crashing, even on VRChat Open Beta with Proton Experimental.)

(NOTE₂: VR mode appears to trigger this audio/video desync crash without requiring any special effort other than the AVPro player beginning playback in the Talent Show world.)

With the recent stable release of VRChat 2023.3.3p1, this crash now happens on VRChat stable, and with Proton 8.x!

So.. technically, this is no longer specific to Open Beta, and it might happen with the stock Steam Deck configuration (unfortunately, I do not have a Steam Deck to test - it is a bit dependent on CPU load/availability).

I've posted a new comment to Valve's Proton issue tracker with VRChat & Proton debug logs for all 8 tested combinations:

https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton/issues/1199#issuecomment-1770336669

On a stock Steam Deck (default Proton, default h264 - not sure if it's unlocked by default on Deck - developer mode enabled), plus the stable version of VRC, I wasn't able to cause a crash in this world with video playing with the mirror or loading a Very Poor non-cached avatar - but I was able to cause one by taking a 4K photo.

I can upload the output log from /home/deck/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/compatdata/438100/pfx/drive_c/users/steamuser/AppData/LocalLow/VRChat/VRChat/ or the crash.dmp file somewhere if needed but the uploader here only seems to support images.

QM build: 1370

Good news!  The root cause of this issue has been tracked down to a race condition in Proton, and there's an open pull request to 'dxvk' to fix it.  I've built a custom Proton version featuring the 'dxvk' patch and it has solved the crashing issues for me, as documented here:

https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton/issues/1199#issuecomment-1813844933

As this *should* be fixed whenever Valve merges in the 'dxvk' code change to Proton and releases that in an update, you can probably mark this feedback entry as fixed.

Dear VRChat employee,

I truly hope you can see and enjoy how much you have helped people care for each other. There are a lot of friends I like to play with, and they have settled on VRChat. As such, I very much want to play on VRChat in order to play with my friends. While the product you have made still has a long way to go, many modelers and scripters have worked together with optimizing programmers towards helping make the wonderous ability to show yourself to others how you want to be in worlds where they want to go. This is a very powerful feature, and I really hope you can get closer. There is clearly a lot of love in the community for helping each other have a lot of fun and comfort. Please, do everything you can to support them, and be careful to make sure you give them room to explore. The mod ban hit them hard, even if you had good intentions.

As a Linux user, however, I have run into more issues than most. Some updates, I have to figure out some combination of SteamVR version and Proton version to get VRC to even launch. Some releases, it seems to work fine on all of them. One recurring issue that has been getting worse, though, is the crashing worlds. I believe it is some video players crashing me constantly.

Via ProtonDB, ( https://www.protondb.com/app/438100 ), in a post titled "AVPro video players don't work", I am offered a launch option "--disable-hw-video-decoding". This seems to fix the crashing worlds. I still miss out on video in those worlds which can severly limit what I am able to get from them, but there were worlds that still used a video player where I could see and hear what is seen and heard by those around me. As of late, however, the last I knew of them no longer work.

Two beautiful worlds with video players that used to work for me and no longer work at all for me are linked.

https://vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_93dc2a1f-60f6-474f-ba8b-f86ad2fd8025

https://vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_3d892cf2-cd4a-4322-9e7e-2ec0cd7ea44c

Right now, there is one scenario where I see even partial functionality. When I join the world, I get to hear music. When I check the video player and show its controls, I see that the mode "Stream" is selected. When I try "Video" mode, it fails to work as all the other players, but the audio-only stream seems to function just fine.

https://vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_65ce4a4b-f66f-4844-adfe-072663394514

I know you may not consider Linux support as a priority issue, but when you see how a company that traps you onto their platform can wantonly mistreat the people you love and keep getting away with it, you may very well know the pain of loss and the desire to build a better future that comes with it. I have personally taken this as a way to try making sure that, for the next wave of people left marooned by a company that thinks they own your experience, there will be a safe, comfortable, and productive place where they can continue being themselves. I know you do not want anyone to feel trapped on your platform, and that you are dealing with your early design decisions and plenty of other issues I am sure I do not know. For my own use, though, I really just want the option to relax with my friends and watch something together. If this is an easy enough fix, it would go a long way towards letting all the other Linux users play without having to go to an external site to find the fix and put in a launch option in a realm of worlds devoid of that bit of life.

Thank you and well wishes,

Green_Dragon_Iris
