details:
Opening this again as https://feedback.vrchat.com/open-beta/p/add-a-public-vrcsdk-api-method-for-silently-invoking-the-constraint-upgrader is not the same issue and was probably inappropriately merged with Fuka's post.

In 3.7.0-beta.1 there is an auto fix for converting existing constraints to VRC Constraints. This enumerates animation clips in the animator controllers attached to the avatar descriptor, and rewrites their curves to match the new constraints. However, it will not be able to identify animations merged using nondestructive utilities. Thus, when the user runs the auto fix, they'll end up with components converted, but animations left unchanged (or vice versa).

While Senky's post is a useful one (we could invoke the converter at build time to help address this issue), being able to invoke the conversion process from our tools does not resolve the issue of the auto fix action, when invoked manually by the end-user from the VRCSDK UI directly, missing animation clips that need adjustment. As such, an API is needed to allow nondestructive tools help the VRCSDK discover any additional animation clips that need to be processed during this manual auto fix invocation.

Note also that both VRCFury and Modular Avatar perform animation path rewriting, so your API will need to be amenable to this as well. MA currently only does prefix rewriting, but I have plans to add more advanced forms of path rewriting in the future.
title: [SDK 3.7.0-beta.1] Please provide a hook for supplying additional animation clips and their relative paths during Auto Fix transformations of constraints

comments.value:
Thanks for the info. I'd like to verify that I've understood this correctly.

When the user uses the menu option VRChat SDK/Utilities/Convert Unity Constraints To VRChat Constraints with one or more prefabs/game objects selected, we should invoke a C# function (System.Func) that MA or VRCF can subscribe to and use to return a set of animation clips to convert. The VRCSDK will then convert only those animation clips instead of attempting to find valid clips itself.

MA/VRCF would subscribe to a C# Func exposed by AvatarDynamicsSetup as the editor starts (for example by using a method with the InitializeOnLoadMethod attribute). The Unity constraint currently being converted and the avatar descriptor found in the current game object or its parents could be provided as parameters. If the function is not subscribed to, we will try to find clips from the avatar descriptor as usual.

Does this sound correct? Is there any other info you would need as part of the function?

Additionally, users can convert individual animation clips in their Unity project directly through this feature - can you confirm whether this would also need support for any special handling?

Also as a bit of context re path rewriting - as far as MA is concerned, any paths in the VRCSDK descriptor refer to the initial (pre-build) state of the avatar. For now. This might not be true forever, if I ever get around to implementing a symlink-like component, but presumably the constraint converter will be less important by then.

@{5c1475afb7ce126e9e0e3a39|full_name} Thanks very much, this is very helpful. I'm assuming in your event example that the `string` in `clipsAndPaths` represents a new path we should assign across all of the curve bindings for this clip (https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/EditorCurveBinding-path.html) during auto-conversion. If the string is null or empty, then we won't modify the path per the default behavior for the VRCSDK. Please let me know if any of that is incorrect.

Based on your comments we can also search the avatar descriptor for animation clips even if a custom collection event function is given, and the results of the two would be combined together ignoring any duplicates.

@{65f4b1a3d0a7a0c657a7d3a8|full_name} Rather, the path would be the path corresponding to the component in question in the clip (thus, if you want to limit your modification to just the one constraint, you can avoid touching other constraints in the same clip). I suppose it might also be good to pass a list or enumerable of components, just so that we can avoid having to walk all of the animator controllers multiple times.

In particular, you would never want to modify the paths in the animation clip - after all, the GameObjects aren't changing. That's MA's job - MA just needs to be able to signal to VRCSDK what paths correspond to the components being modified.
Also, it would be really appreciated if you could preview the specific final API with Senky and I before throwing it out in a full release that has to be supported forever onward 😅

@{5c1475afb7ce126e9e0e3a39|full_name}I think the event could be something like: 

`public static event void CollectReferencedAnimations(object sender, CollectReferencedAnimationsEventArgs e)`

which stores everything inside of it as a class from above that has `get; set;` on most of the properties inside of it. This is how I do events to keep things very simple.

Also then the default VRChat handling *could* then also use this event as well and everything would be wonderful for everyone.

From writing .NET code for years this is how events *should* be written (according to the .NET Team at Microsoft), everything they expect the event to edit should have `set` on the properties in the EventArgs class for the event and then the sender of it should then (after event returns) obtain the value(s) from the event args object for it.

@{5c1475afb7ce126e9e0e3a39|full_name}

> Rather, the path would be the path corresponding to the component in question in the clip

Apologies if I'm misinterpreting this, but since a curve binding path gives the path to the containing game object in the hierarchy, that wouldn't be enough information to identify the constraint component affected by this curve since a game object can have multiple constraints of different types on it. You would need the type of constraint in addition to that to identify the component affected by the curve. This is why the currently proposed interface gives a single Unity constraint component, since it allows us to map from each component to the set of animation clips associated with it.

> Also, it would be really appreciated if you could preview the specific final API with Senky and I before throwing it out in a full release that has to be supported forever onward

We're discussing the viability of private SDK builds internally now.

I’ll also mention that both me and Senky are considering ways to auto convert the entire avatar, nondestructively at build time, which avoids numerous problems with the auto fix approach. As a general rule MA won’t do something unless the user opts in, but I could see a world where auto fix just adds a “MA Convert Constraints” to the avatar root, given the right VRCSDK hooks.

Due to the risk of breaking prefabs I'm now more inclined to patch auto fix to use a nondestructive method of conversion rather than participate in destructive conversion of existing animations; the above IVRCConstraintConversionProvider strategy would help avoid the need for using Harmony for this.

(Or you could provide a nondestructive component yourself...)

@{5c1475afb7ce126e9e0e3a39|full_name}  @{5fa08ddb2644fb4c5a3dfe75|full_name}

After reviewing this further and based on the comments here, we're now looking at replacing this with a simpler delegate event that's invoked once as we begin the process of converting to VRChat constraints, or in other words as soon as the user presses the Auto-Fix button or uses the equivalent menu entries. It would have a signature like this:

`public delegate bool ConvertUnityConstraintsOnGameObjectsDelegate(List<GameObject> gameObjects);`

The list of game objects is simply the set of game objects selected by the user, or the game object containing the avatar descriptor of the current avatar if the auto-fix option is used.

The return value tells us if the VRCSDK should go attempt its own conversion or not. If you return true, we'll immediately stop on the assumption that conversion has been handled by a user integrated tool instead - the warning dialog wouldn't be shown either. If false is returned or nothing is subscribed to the event, we'll continue with the built-in converter as usual. If there are multiple subscribers, we'll run all of them and abort the SDK's converter if any of them have returned true.

This will allow you to implement your own handling of this problem without any intervention from the VRCSDK.

Note that we also allow users to right click on individual animation clips in the project window and convert those individually. We'll expose a similar delegate event for this as well, in case it's needed:

`public delegate bool ConvertUnityConstraintsOnAnimationClipsDelegate(List<AnimationClip> animationClips);`

Again, the list would contain the clips selected for conversion by the user, and we would abort from the SDK if true is returned.

Please let us know if the above is correct or if further changes are needed. Regarding previewing this before it goes live, we are planning to release a beta SDK with these changes for you to review.

Additionally:

- If a delegate throws an exception, we will log it and then intepret it as a signal not to run the SDK's converter.

- We are exposing the methods to convert a set of animation clips (`ConvertUnityConstraintTracksToVrChatConstraintTracks()`) and apply rebinding to a single animation clip (`RebindConstraintAnimationClip()`) in case they're needed.

@{65f4b1a3d0a7a0c657a7d3a8|full_name}

I'd recommend the addition of one more delegate:

```

public delegate bool AreUnityConstraintsAutoConverted(List<GameObject> gameObjects);

```

The intent for this is to suppress the auto fix message (and quest build block) if the conversion is being handled in a non-destructive way (ie - if there is a configuration to convert these constraints at build time). If this is not implemented, I intend to perform Harmony patching to suppress the message, but it would be preferable to have this be a supported API.

Alternately:

```

public delegate bool IsUnityConstraintAutoConverted(IConstraint constraint);

```

(this one is probably easier to avoid MA and VRCF stepping on each other's toes...)

@{5c1475afb7ce126e9e0e3a39|full_name} I've added your second suggestion. It will be called for every Unity constraint we detect on the avatar before the validation message is displayed. If true is returned for all of them, the validation message won't appear.
@{65f4b1a3d0a7a0c657a7d3a8|full_name} that sounds perfect, thanks! Once the beta SDK is out I’ll put together a MA patch to address things on my side.

Quick feedback - I think we need separate callbacks for "user invoked auto fix" vs "user tried to convert via the VRChat SDK -> Utilities option" vs "a script tried to convert this". I think only the auto fix one really needs to be overridden here.
https://github.com/bdunderscore/modular-avatar/pull/1010 here's the implementation I'm considering, for your reference

@{5c1475afb7ce126e9e0e3a39|full_name}

Thanks, I'm pleased to see you've been able to integrate with this.

> I think we need separate callbacks for "user invoked auto fix" vs "user tried to convert via the VRChat SDK -> Utilities option" vs "a script tried to convert this"

To avoid creating too many delegates, we could instead pass an additional boolean parameter to `OnConvertUnityConstraintsOnGameObjects` to indicate if this was triggered by the user clicking auto-fix or not. You'd be able to return immediately if it's false.

@{5c1475afb7ce126e9e0e3a39|full_name}  @{5fa08ddb2644fb4c5a3dfe75|full_name}

Heads up, we will be renaming some of these symbols in the next version of the SDK. We're doing this to try and simplify their names a bit and make it clearer which of these display modal dialogs and can be affected by external tooling, since it would be a lot more difficult to do this after the SDK is live.

was renamed to

was renamed to

was renamed to

details:
__Pros:__

- `gesture_wheel_stay` is neat as it fixes an issue when moving to prevent gestures from being activated when rotating on the right hand.

__Cons:__

- Open Hand is unbound, even though `gesture_wheel_cancel` is supposed to do open hand; it is okay that `gesture_wheel_cancel` is not auto bound to open hand for the purposes of other controller types and the existence of chords.

- `gesture_wheel_cancel`: Trigger Held + Grip Double Click

details:
From digging, it appears that `ConvertUnityConstraintsToVrChatConstraints` requires or looks for an avatar descriptor to modify animations of. We could benefit from public function that doesn't touch animators or look at animations and **purely** converts constraint components.

(So we'll have the counterpart to `ConvertUnityConstraintTracksToVrChatConstraintTracks` which only modifies animations)
title: [3.7.0-beta.2 SDK] Simple Conversion For constraints

comments.value:
`ConvertUnityConstraintsToVrChatConstraints` is called by various parts of the SDK (auto-fix and context menu items) and accepts a list of game objects - these don't need to be VRChat avatars. You can create normal prefabs with Unity constraints on them and right click them to convert them, which calls this method with all of the selected prefabs. This method normally tries to convert animation clips as well since otherwise you'd end up with clips containing orphaned tracks.

We already expose an overload of this method (a variant with the same name but different parameters) that runs without displaying any modal dialog and no undo support. It accepts an array of Unity constraints, an optional avatar descriptor to check for animation clips in, and a boolean that lets you skip clip conversion entirely. I think the third parameter is what you'd want to use here.

Would that let you achieve what you're aiming for?

@{65f4b1a3d0a7a0c657a7d3a8|full_name} Attempting to use `ConvertUnityConstraintsToVrChatConstraint` with a Game Object list has it iterate through parents of the provided objects for a VRCAvatarDescriptor to modify animations. It could probably use an extra bool parameter to skip the entire descriptor check & warning popup. 

I'll try making a tool with the IConstraints[] variant of the function and get back to you.

@{5f2e0a4e8464150716ffd322|full_name} That's right, you can avoid the automated search for an avatar descriptor by using the IConstraint[] overload. You'd want to provide null as the avatar descriptor if you're skipping clip conversion.

The challenge with adding new parameters here is that tools like VRCFury and Modular Avatar need to be able to hook into this process to run their own variant of it, potentially replacing the SDK's implementation. Any new parameters added to the main interface method would therefore also need to be implemented by those tools, which can't be guaranteed.

@{65f4b1a3d0a7a0c657a7d3a8|full_name} Oh! I didn't realize I could provide null without breaking it. https://github.com/ZenithVal/Zenis-Unity-Tools/blob/main/VRCConstraintConversion.cs 

Thanks! This can be closed.

@{5f2e0a4e8464150716ffd322|full_name} Yes, we only try searching the avatar descriptor's animation layers when looking for clips to convert. If this is null, we fall back to searching for an Animator component with an assigned controller instead. In your case neither of those will happen since the third parameter is set to false.

Just to let you know since you're writing custom code to interact with the converter already, these symbols will be renamed in a future version of the SDK since it's still technically in beta at the moment. These changes will be reflected in our documentation, but I've also summarized the renames in this other Canny here (you'll need to scroll down a bit): https://feedback.vrchat.com/open-beta/p/sdk-370-beta1-please-provide-a-hook-for-supplying-additional-animation-clips-and

@{65f4b1a3d0a7a0c657a7d3a8|full_name} In the meantime I have another avatar that is experiencing different behaviors between auto-conversion and normal conversion, should I post it here too or would a new canny be best?

@{6075548fb0c5603e04a7fe69|full_name} If it's the same issue with network synced drones then feel free to share them here, otherwise it would be best to create a new Canny with a description of that separate problem.

I've traced this to what might be a setup issue on this specific avatar, because I can see differences between this avatar and a new one created using Custom Object Sync and then converted to VRChat constraints with no other changes.

The game object named Custom Object Sync needs to be at the origin of the world with no rotation and regular scale. On this avatar, I can see that this game object is using a VRChat parent constraint and scale constraint both with no sources and Freeze To World enabled. This doesn't match what normally happens, where the game object is instead constrainted to a prefab with a position and rotation of (0, 0, 0) and a scale of (1, 1, 1). The current setup means the game object will take on the initial position, rotation and scale of the avatar when it appears instead, which may also be slightly different for each user in the instance with you.

Could you please try the following to help eliminate this as a potential cause? You may want to back up your project first.

1. Create a new game object at the root of the scene in your avatar project, setting its position and rotation to (0, 0, 0) and its scale to (1, 1, 1).

2. Create a prefab of this game object, then delete the original instance in the scene.

3. On the parent constraint on the Custom Object Sync game object on your avatar, untick Freeze To World under advanced settings and assign the prefab you've just created as a source with a weight of 1 and no offsets.

4. Do this with the scale constraint on that game object as well.

5. Rebuild and retry with this avatar in-game to see if this solves the issue, then report back here.

The behavior of Freeze To World is documented here: https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/avatar-dynamics/constraints/#freeze-to-world

@{65f4b1a3d0a7a0c657a7d3a8|full_name} Just did exactly this, turns out it was indeed the issue! I had assumed having a prefab with 0,0,0 position and 1,1,1 scale would produce the exact same result as having no sources and checking "Freeze to World".

Maybe adding a little sentence in the documentation about this would be useful but regardless thanks a lot for helping me deal with this! I will be sharing that to other creators encountering similar issues due to this assumption.
@{6075548fb0c5603e04a7fe69|full_name} Thanks! We'll review the documentation. Marking this Canny as Closed for now since this was traced to the avatar itself.

details:
The `Offline for` time reported in the client appears to be based on the user's last reported login time, rather than the user's last reported activity time, which typically corresponds to the last reported interaction with any part of the VRChat client. In some of the images provided below, the user was last online `3 hours ago`, but the client reports the time as `8 hours ago`, reflecting their last reported login time.

There are some inconsistencies here, and additional API endpoints may be needed to accurately report when a user was last online, rather than relying on `Last Login` or `Last Activity`.
title: 'Offline for' time reported in-client based off last login instead of last activity

comments.value: Basically, using `Last Login` to report the user's `Offline For` time can be highly inaccurate compared to when the user *actually* went offline.

I understand, however, that a caveat to this is that `Last Activity` is reported every time any activity is detected, whether it's on the website or in Unity, as reported by the SDK.

Although to be fair, `Last Login` also updates if logging into the website or SDK.
Definitely can be very inaccurate for those of us who are on for 10+ hours at a time.

Another example of the significant time discrepancy: The client is reporting this person as offline since yesterday at 15:34 (23 hours ago, their previous login time), but they actually went offline less than an hour ago as of this post.
How?, last activity isn't the same as last game logged in time (open beta notes)

I've got several versions of the same avatar which use the same body model (they have different outfits), and use a number of constraints for body shaping/deform (twist bones, muscles, shaping, etc).  So to make my life easy, I put a bunch of VRC Rotation Constraints in a prefab, just like I do with my physbone settings.

Unlike physbones though, this is a source of great frustration.

The #1 issue is going in and out of playmode seems to randomly deactivate one or more of the constraints - which one seems to be different for each avatar, but it's 100% reproducible for a given avatar.

Another issue I noticed was trying to apply or revert prefab settings - a reproducible case is to have two rotation constraints on a single GameObject in a prefab, activate both, then try to apply or revert any setting for one of the constraints while watching the other one - you'll note it has some settings change unintentionally. Bumping this feedback request because I'm very adamant that this needs to be a thing before this feature goes live.

I'm noticing multiple instances of people opting into the beta, not realizing this feature is on by default, and feeling really embarrassed that they've been making typos and drafting responses they never intended for people to see because there is zero indication of this being a thing inside the keyboard itself.

details:
When using auto-send on the chatbox, messages persist even when the message is fully deleted.

I believe this behaviour is strange because when using auto-type, you're expecting what's inside the chatbox to mirror what's on top of your head at all times. This is likely a bug when referring to deleting the message, but I've marked this as a feature request because I also believe that this should be the case when closing the chatbox.

When the chatbox is closed, the message inside is erased, therefore it should be removed from your head. The message not getting deleted when the chatbox is closed creates a dissonance between what the player is able to intuitively know about what's on top of their head.

**Proposed behaviour:**

- Closing the chatbox with a message inside and auto-send enabled makes the message disappear after a few seconds, regardless of chatbox duration settings.

- Erasing the text inside the chatbox with auto-send enabled makes the message disappear instantly.

- Manually hitting "Send" with auto-send enabled ignores these behaviours and behaves identically to a manually-sent message. (Respects "chatbox duration" setting.)
title: [1511] Chatbox messages sent through auto-send should disappear when the message is erased or the chatbox is closed

details:
A simplified version of the keyboard input field has been added in Build 1511.

This simplified input field is the default display on mobile, desktop, and Pico platforms.

In mechanisms that involve copy and paste functions, such as entering URLs for videos or images, outputting world save data or generated content to the InputField, and copying them, the copy and paste buttons are extremely important.

I believe that the absence of these buttons in the default display significantly reduces usability.

Please add copy and paste buttons to the simplified input field, as shown in the attached image.

* This was written using a translation tool.

In previous versions, turning on flying mode would lock the roll of the camera lens to the horizon. In the latest beta, the lens now rolls to match how you're holding the camera. This makes it very difficult to take level photos/videos

This could be fixed by either restoring the old roll-snapping of flying mode (maybe in 90° increments so it works with portrait orientation), or changing the auto-level behavior to only lock roll instead of locking roll and pitch.

details:
The "Show Additional Information on Nameplates" option seems to have changed behaviour: nameplates now always appear when the quick menu is open regardless of any other settings. Not sure if it's a bug or intended change.

It used to be that if nameplates were hidden and that option was disabled, nameplates would not appear even when opening the quick menu. This was great for immersion and allowed for a more natural social experience at times.

Now nameplates always appear when opening the quick menu. No combination of settings prevents that (for me, at least. Someone else claimed they got it working somehow? I tried for quite a while with no success)

The new behaviour is more consistent with the tooltip description but I miss not having a more immersive mode.

A new "Don't show nameplates when opening the quick menu" toggle would be ideal if there's no interest in restoring old behaviour.
title: [1512] No longer possible to fully hide nameplates

details:
I think it would be interesting if instead of letting us make stickers that animate freely, they animate depending on the angle you're viewing them from, aka lenticular stickers.

I was discussing with friends the possibility of having animated stickers, but I argued that having animated stickers would make the sticker system more obtrusive and less "grounded in physicality" than I assume the VRC team is trying to make them.

Having the animation of stickers be handled this way would mean that they only animate upon the player moving parallel to it, which would be much less jarring and eye-catching when placed in a world. For example, seeing a sticker animating by itself in the background would be eye-catching and jarring, whereas seeing a lenticular sticker would appear as a normal sticker (except maybe shinier or something?) unless the player begins moving around it.

I think this would be a really elegant way of giving people their much requested "animated stickers" while maintaining the sticker system's physicality and unobtrusive nature.
title: [1514] Add lenticular stickers (Stickers that animate based on viewing angle)

details:
When using hand tracking in PC VRChat, I noticed that some incorrect animator tracking control settings in Gesture Animator may results some not expected behavior. 

Details:

1. As the first screenshot, if you toggle "Animation" for left fingers in Animator Tracking Control, when user trigger a gesture on left controller in VRChat client, avatar will play a hand animation on hand skeletions;

2. As the second screenshot, if you toggle "Tracking" for left fingers in Animator Tracking Control, when user trigger a gesture on left controller in VRChat client, avatar will keep following with the skeleton data and plays a gesture;

How does this feature relate to the topic of hand tracking?

- As my personal reseach with avatars, normally, most avatars is "animation" in gesture controller layers (same scenario as the first screenshot).  And this breaked the visual experience of hand tracking.

- When using hand tracking with VD, avatar fingers play gesture animation when I trigger a gesture, but as I expected it should keep following my fingers and plays nothing;

- After I toggle "Tracking" for all fingers in VRC Animator Tracking Control, and re-upload my avatar, it behaves normal and keep following with my fingers when I trigger a gesture animation. 

Why not we just let the skeleton inputs directly override those animation behavior in gesture animator? 

The reason I believe this is necessary:

1. Most users owned a Meta Quest 2 or 3, and it has a good experience with hand tracking. This feature will be a big goods for these users. As is, multiple manufactors are developing gloves, PCVR users will need it too. 

2. It's very easy to make a work around in Unity, just modify Animator Tracking Control settings, but when we considering that many users still using public avatars, is not possible to ask them fix this by themselves.

3. It could be a option in client, same as "FBT Locomotion Animation" in FBT settings. We can disable it in avatar descriptor, but also users can cancel it in client.
title: [ input 2.0 ] Support hand tracking skeleton inputs override gesture animations

comments.value: Update 1 : My friend tell me that I can simply disable avatar gesture in MainMenu / Settings / Avatar. Ah… sounds it should can be work. But also it means I can't use gesture emote anyway.

Thank you for the detailed report. As you've noted it's true that you are able to avoid this by disabling gestures, but it's also true that this will disable everything that depends on the gesture parameters. Because our default SDK example doesn't have tracking control state behaviors on the hand states, for now we consider that these were added manually by creators and the function of the tracking control is to override tracking with animation if specified, so this would be considered working as intended.

It's understandable that creators may have been setting the tracking control to override with animation due to the lower fidelity of skeletal tracking available in the past (not expecting high fidelity hand tracking for creating accurate poses like peace sign with finger spread etc) and so they felt the need to override with animation, and so this is a new situation now that higher fidelity skeletal tracking may be becoming more normal. We'll continue to observe if this requires some new custom behavior, so thank you for creating this feedback post.

For the near term we consider the tracking control when set to override tracking with animation as working as intended. So for now the recommended action would be either to disable gestures or to upload the avatar without setting tracking control to animation.

details:
Transparency is hard and VRChat cannot control all conditions a user can place a sticker down in.

Most stickers do not need to be transparent; whilst the funniest and best stickers _are_, as users have quickly discovered that the best way to use a sticker is to slap a modifier on someone else's, most stickers are going to be one or more opaque forms on a transparent background.

As such, VRChat could allow for a user to place either a transparent or non-transparent (cutout?) version of a sticker they've created down. This would allow for a good level of flexibility. This might also be a vector for performance, with distant stickers that are not occluded being swapped to cutout to help lower pixel overdraw.
title: [Stickers] Allow toggling the shader used for a sticker between a transparent and an opaque or cutout shader to help solve transparency woes

comments.value:
Extra notes: For a cutout variant, a custom shader could be written that could give borders of the opaque islands a white outline, like real stickers.

For UI/UX, I'd encourage updating the dropper UI anyway to make it clearer to the user what the sticker will look like when dropped. As part of this, a small pop-up saying "transparent" that you flip to "opaque" via a button press is displayed. The user can see the difference looking at the preview that the dropper tool is providing.

details:
I am writing to express my strong dissatisfaction with the recent update to the video player in public instances. The decision to restrict video playback to only whitelisted domains is a significant step backward and will negatively impact the creativity and enjoyment of many users.

While I understand the need to prevent the playback of malicious content, this blanket restriction is overly broad and disproportionate. It unfairly penalizes content creators who rely on embedding videos from various platforms to enhance their worlds. Additionally, it limits the ability of users to discover new and interesting content.

I propose the following alternatives:

Implement a more granular content filtering system. This could involve using a combination of blacklists, whitelists, and content analysis to identify and block harmful content.

Provide users with more control over their video playback settings. This could include the ability to allow or block specific domains, as well as adjust the playback quality and size.

Educate users about the risks of playing untrusted content. This could be done through in-game messages, tutorials, and community forums.

By adopting these suggestions, the developers can effectively address the security concerns without stifling creativity and innovation.

I urge you to reconsider this decision and work towards a more balanced approach that benefits both creators and users.
title: [1546]Request for Reconsideration of Recent Changes to Video Playback Permissions

it may be a slightly different issue, but it (redownloading content that i definitely had cached in my 200GB of cache) happened to me only the first time i loaded each piece of content in the beta.

something seem to have changed with cache file paths, and the folder containing the specific version of the avatar is now named differently, so the file was "missing" and had to be redownloaded

the __data files in both of the folders in the attachments below are identical.

for clarity obviously i haven't modified this avatar in the meantime

@{654a7d1f1870ff9faf0911e8|full_name} 

oh, it took me a minute after writing the above standalone comment, but i believe i know what causes it.

previously cache folders were created in an alphabetical order, so tools removing older versions had to keep just the "greatest" one after sorting them by name.

now this naming system changed (see my above screenshots) and it may cause the newer version's folder to be alphabetically "earlier"/"lower", so the aforementioned tools delete it, causing it to be missing and getting redownloaded during the next session.

cheers.

STR:

1. take a photo

2. print it out

3. start editing its caption/custom message

4. ask someone to grab the print that you're editing

5. submit the new caption

what should've happened:

6. the new caption gets saved and synchronized among everyone in the instance

what happens:

6. nothing

Looks like the prints use a system akin to Udon's networking ownership, and when you grab a print you become its owner, so then the person submitting a new caption doesn't have the 'right' to request sync of the new value.

PS: if the other person drops the print, and you grab it before clicking save/submit/however it's called, the new caption syncs just fine, probably because you're the networking owner of the print again.

details:
Currently, on live, it is possible to see a significant portion of someone's chatbox over the main menu. If you wanted to browse your avatars or find a new world to hop to, it was possible to still see what they were saying if they were unable to speak at the time. You'd also be in a position where you're still looking mostly at the person.

However, on beta, almost all of the top margin is now taken up. You could point your camera at the ceiling and use the bottom margin, but from the other person's PoV, you're no longer looking at them and able to see their chatbox.

I think a good and simple solution to this would be to lower the menu and re-center it, so the bottom and top margins are the same again. EDIT: Per the VRChat Discord, the room at the bottom of the menu is to accommodate three lines of tooltips. So, the only other thing I can think of currently would be to allow the menu to be resized. Or perhaps add a button to collapse/expand the new menu header, as is done with the wings.

I phrase this as an accessibility concern because you can still hear someone talking to you behind the main menu. If the person in front of you was muted when you pulled up the main menu and was un-muted when the menu was dismissed, this would be very inconvenient. For someone who physically cannot speak without using a chatbox, this is essentially what's happening to them now.

I've included screenshots of the difference.

details:
The new log file format is missing a unique delimiter to separate log entries.

The log file format was changed from having `"\n\n\r\n"` as its log entry delimiter to `"\r\n"`. This is an issue because there are log entries that contain `"\r\n"` in them, meaning that it is now impossible to read log files using a tailing function.

The only workaround I can think of right now, is to not release a log entry from my function until I know the next line in the file is the beginning of a new log entry. This has the drawback of always being one log entry behind in the log, preventing you from reading the latest log entry.

My suggestion would be to remove all carriage return chars (`'\r'`) from the log entry strings. This would make the log entry delimiter of `"\r\n"` unique, and it would remove some unnecessary characters from from the files. A log reading program can then easily replace all `"\n"` with `"\r\n"` to restore the original log strings after reading the log file.

Alternatively, add a unique delimiter char at the end of each log entry, but that would add length to the file rather than reduce it. And you could still have worlds that log that unique delimiter char using the `Debug.Log(string)` function. So the idea of removing carriage return chars just seems simpler and cleaner.
title: [1582] New Log File Format Delimiter Issue

comments.value: I would prefere escaping of log messages instead of altering the log message, like `\r` => `\\r` `\n`=>`\\n`. we might find some other characters which need to be escaped too.

@{60e65f577ae9d0492b0f2a75|full_name}, That is a very good point actually. That might be a better solution.

But it would make the raw text file harder to read by newbies, with just `"\n"` it might at least still show as new lines, depending on the text program.

@{610d538d5303a82960a415b4|full_name} why would you let newbies read such complex log files?

They would probably only forward it to you/me/others

We aren't planning to change the formatting of our log files at this time. Condensing these files makes it easier to debug issues with them, which is their main purpose. We'd rather not risk modifying written messages, since we're aware of some worlds that read the log file back again that may depend on exact characters making their way into the log file as written.

Regarding your use case, if you're monitoring the file while VRChat is actively writing to it, I feel you should be able to read to the end of the file to find the most recent log statement? VRChat will only write whole log statements each time it updates the file.

@{65f4b1a3d0a7a0c657a7d3a8|full_name}, This is an understandable reason. I would however nitpick correct you by saying that a world can't read the log file, only external applications can and some indeed do and they already have to change because of these changes.

The whole point of the Open Beta is to test this and see how it works, so we are giving feedback on how this right now is making some issues. It isn't live yet.

Could also change the log entry delimiter to `"\r\r\n"`, since the extra carriage return char would likely be ignored by most text programs, and it would make the log entry delimiter easier to detect programmatically.

details:
1. Switch camera mode to stream, enable spout output. Switch dolly mode to multi.

2. Send 3 camera points - 0 + 1 path index 0, 2 path index 1.

3. Hit start - you will see the path 1 camera duplicate, stuck to the user's local space. It will also lag more and more the more you create. Hitting start/stop in-game - even if you don't wait for the countdown to finish - will result in cloning the camera into your viewport.

This also prevents Spout from properly deactivating the cameras on stop - Spout continues to broadcast the viewpoint of the cameras from the last time you hit play after it has stopped. The broken cameras do not broadcast, but given the lag, I assume they still have an active camera on anyway.

Every time you stop/start, you will create another duplicate.

Switching to single, and even switching instance will not remove the bad cameras. You need to fully restart the game to get rid of them.

In some cases, depending on setup, this can also lock out the ability to change camera mode - even when dolly is stopped. Again, this persists across instance switches, and requires a full game restart to fix.

Minimal JSON to load to cause the issue for automated testing - but this is able to be accomplished in-game:

```

[{"PathIndex": 0}, {"PathIndex": 0}, {"PathIndex": 1}]

```

You can add `"IsLocal": true` to all of these to make it easier to see (and is what I did in the attached example)

The attached video and image was done over OSC, but this was separately confirmed that it can be accomplished with no external tools.

details:
When swapping Pins, the cam takes on the properties set on the Pin. However, when utilizing the Dolly between Pins, the Paths attempt to recreate the cam settings, breaking the Path. 

Would it be possible to create an alternative mode to Paths that links a singular Path behavior to a Pin similarly to a standalone Pin's behavior? 

The intention would be that swapping Pins would allow for the same 3 real-time camera Paths (i.e. the "Multi" Streaming setting) just attached to each individual Pin without breaking the Path.

Use Case #1 

A streamed event or podcast that has one rotating Path around the MC on Pin 1, a slow in-and-out Path activated on Pin 2, and a basic static cam for Pin 3. 

Use Case #2

A game show that has 3 preset Paths set up that show players on different parts of a map that can be swapped between via Pins. 

To go even further, if Import Paths were implemented, a production team could theoretically preset all their Paths in advance for moment-to-moment swapping across each Pin.

Hopefully this makes sense and will be considered for the more real-time event-oriented creators.
title: [Dolly] [1583] Standalone Path linked to a single Pin

details:
Artificial Horizons/Altitude Indicators are a common staples of both real life aircrafts and drones along with various simulators. It would be nice for the newly added VRChat drone to also reflect this common tool.

For context an Altitude indicator or Artificial horizon is the orange/blue ball showing the tilt of an aircraft or the degree indicators used in a game like Elite Dangerous when trying to land on a planet. As far as incorporating it into VRChat, this could be an overlay like the grid we already have or it can be rendered on the edge of the controller or FPV mode.

As far as the benefit of this addition, as a lot of players would be newer to flying FPV drones (even more so in VR), this would help keep track of the drone's current state. Currently the drone can be a little awkward to control given the camera tilt's adjustable state. I personally find it difficult to stay level with auto centering off since my only point of reference is if my drone is drifting in any direction.

Video of an irl drone using a full INAV which includes the Artificial Horizon

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g9DnYqldCxE

Included are also photos of a real life altitude indicator, and the Elite Dangerous UI display for landing on planets.
title: [1601] Drone could use an Artificial Horizon UI

details:
On the drone there seems to be a drag model based on the drones velocity vector as respects to the orientation of the drone. This a rad feature as you would feel more drag when the drone is flat compared to the drone being sideways.

I believe the difference between the drag coefficient of the least exposed surface area to most exposed area is too high.

For instance, if you are falling sideways you gain significant speed which feels alright, but once you flip your drone flat out of that fall, it's like you pulled a parachute.

Video for reference: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P13cuSiHPGg

The over exaggerated drag is also affecting thrust performance as well as the ability to maintain momentum.

I can see the use case of having such high and significant drag for filming and the use case of people that are using the drone more as a toy and less as a performance machine. Therefore the ability to adjust this coefficient could be very rad. I understand that there is already a drag slider, but the addition of this editable coefficient could open up more use cases for the drone.
title: Build: 1602, Drone Drag Coefficient Feels Off

comments.value: 100% agreed with everything above. Drag being more closely aligned to what it is supposed to be will open up the ability for more robust freestyle maneuvers, increasing the drone's longevity in the community of people that wish to use this frequently.

I'll actually note after maxing out drag it feels like both sides could be too extreme. Max drag and minimum mass it still drops out of the air EXTREMELY FAST when dropping the drone sideways out of the sky. I think we need to have the the minimum surface area drag increased and the maximum surface area drag decreased

details:
Access to additional physics parameters already existing in the drone flight system could be beneficial to curating ones perfect flying experience. Additional parameters could include.

-the strength of gravity

comments.value: This. Or a parameter like for earmuff mode would also be nice!
can confirm this should not be a feature. this is a serious privacy risk.

Enable FPV indicator requires a penetrating means of notification to both the takeoff point and the drone's current position. Also, the idea of ​​leaving the visibility of the drone to the viewing/listening side is flawed.

This is because disabling the first drone and not noticing the arrival of subsequent drones poses a privacy risk that could allow for unintentional eavesdropping.

Some may be of the opinion that conversations that would be embarrassing to be overheard should be held in a private instance, but in order to prevent unintentional recordings by the person being overheard or leaks of team strategies during a competition, controlling instance permissions alone is not enough.

I think we should not forget that VRChat also has an aspect of a gaming platform.

Enable FPV インジケーターは離陸地点とドローンの現在位置の両方の側に貫通的な手段での通知が必要です。また、見る/聞こえる側にドローンの見え方をゆだねるという考え方には欠陥があります。

details:
Being able to use your own drone 3D model could be really nice and add more variety in game :)

It'd also allow to have "drones" that could be animals, robots or such too for example :)

An easy way could be to check for the presence of a special unity object named "drone" in the avatar's hierarchy.

That way it doesn't require complicated things like introducing new drone polygons limits or such, 

as it'd be already part of the avatar and so counted in the existing avatar limits. 

Simple logic could be that If such a node exists, then load / replace the drone model by the 3D model under the avatar object to display as a drone.

(scaling it down eventually to fit / attach it to the drone "hitbox" and respect the current existing drone physics. ) 

Being able to have a different model per avatar would be super versatile, 

like if you have a dragon avatar, the drone could be a little dragon flying around and so on :)

That would really be neat and add variety and also allow us to finally "fly" in game with a mini avatar / drone of our choice ;)

details:
Typically, drone flight controllers (such as BetaFlight) use three distinct rate settings: "RC Rate," "RC Expo," and "Super Rate." In VRChat's drone system, "Rate" corresponds to "RC Rate," and "Expo" corresponds to "RC Expo." However, "Center Sensitivity" does not correspond to "Super Rate." Instead, it behaves similarly to "RC Expo," mainly affecting sensitivity near the center stick position.

"Super Rate" usually refers to adjusting angular velocity as the stick moves closer to its maximum deflection. This discrepancy between standard drone settings and VRChat’s drone controls can cause confusion when adjusting flight characteristics.

For a more intuitive setup experience, we suggest either aligning VRChat’s drone rate settings more closely with standard drone configurations (such as those used by BetaFlight) or adding clear explanations for each setting parameter.

Flight Presetsの設定項目である「Expo」と「Center Sensitivity」は、どちらもスティック中央付近の感度調整に関連しており、設定内容が重複しています。

一般的なドローン（BetaFlight等）のレート設定では、「RC Rate」「RC Expo」「Super Rate」という3つの項目があります。VRChatのドローン機能では、「Rate」が「RC Rate」、「Expo」が「RC Expo」に対応していますが、「Center Sensitivity」は「Super Rate」に相当していません。現状の「Center Sensitivity」はむしろ「RC Expo」と同様に、スティック中央付近の感度調整に近い内容になっています。

「Super Rate」とは、本来スティックを端まで倒したときの角速度を調整する設定項目です。そのため、実際のドローン設定とVRChatのドローン設定の間にズレがあり、設定が分かりにくくなっています。

より直感的に設定を行うためには、VRChatのドローンのレート設定を一般的なドローン（BetaFlight）の設定項目に近づけるか、もしくは各設定項目について明確な説明を追加することを希望します。
title: [1602]In the Flight Presets, the settings "Expo" and "Center Sensitivity" both relate to sensitivity adjustments around the stick's center area, causing overlap between these two parameters.

details:
In standard drone flight terminology, enabling "Self Leveling" corresponds to the "ANGLE" flight mode. The "HORIZON" mode, in contrast, typically allows unlimited angles based on stick input and behaves as an intermediate mode between "ANGLE" and "ACRO." This does not match the current behavior of VRChat's drone implementation.

Therefore, it would be more accurate to label the flight mode as "ANGLE" when "Self Leveling" is enabled.

ドローンの飛行モードの表示について、現在は「Self Leveling」が有効な場合に「HORIZON」と表示され、無効な場合に「ACRO」と表示されていますが、この表記は正しくありません。

一般的なドローンのモード設定では、「Self Leveling」が有効な場合のモードは「ANGLE」と呼ばれます。「HORIZON」モードは、本来スティック操作による角度制限がなく、「ANGLE」と「ACRO」の中間的な挙動を示すモードであり、現在のVRChatドローンの挙動とは異なっています。

このため、「Self Leveling」が有効な場合の表示は、「ANGLE」とするのが適切だと思われます。
title: [1602]Regarding the drone's flight mode display: currently, when "Self Leveling" is enabled, the mode is displayed as "HORIZON," and when disabled, as "ACRO." However, this labeling is incorrect.

details:

details:
If a finger collider is placed on a bone with a 0 0 0 local position (meaning its world position matches that of the parent), it no longer works in game at all.

This is a regression compared to live, where the finger contact is generated as a sphere at the given location. Moving the child transform even the slightest amount (0.001) resolves the issue.

This is a large breakage, as VRCF global colliders default to 0 height (sphere) by default, and this issue breaks all existing uploaded avatars using that feature.
title: [1602] Spherical finger colliders no longer work at all

comments.value: You can temporarily work around this issue by ensuring that the "height" setting on your VRCF global colliders is a tiny bit greater than two times what you set the radius to.

details:
Turns out that Gesture Manager is broken in the Beta SDK 3.7.7-beta.1 due to some changes in the handling of Unity.Mathematics.

This can only be fixed in Gesture Manager by adding the Assembly Definitions for `Unity.Mathematics` and `Unity.Mathematics.Editor` in the file `vrchat.blackstartx.gesture-manager.editor.asmdef`.

Now, this is an easy fix for Gesture Manager. However, for it to be done in 3.7 is not okay. Because of this breaking change, the SDK Beta 3.7.7 should be changed to 3.8.0!
title: [3.7.7-beta.1] Changes to Unity.Mathematics should invoke SDK 3.8.0 instead.

comments.value: the project developer " gesture menager "  is aware of the bug and is preparing a patch

Actually almost nothing was changed about Unity.Mathmatics but API changes in CollisionScene.ShapeData were made in 3.7.7 beta.

The type of CollisionScene.ShapeData.outPos0 / CollisionScene.ShapeData.outPos1 was UnityEngine.Vector3 but now it is Unity.Mathmatics.float3.

There are some other similar breaking changes around Avatar Dynamics in 3.7.7 beta includes (non-exhaustive):

- VRC.Dynamics.CollisionScene+TransformData.lastPosition removal

- VRC.Dynamics.CollisionScene+TransformData.lastRotation removal

- VRC.Dynamics.CollisionScene+TransformData.position UnityEngine.Vector3 -> Unity.Mathmatics.float3

- VRC.Dynamics.CollisionScene+TransformData.rotation UnityEngine.Quaternion -> Unity.Mathmatics.quaternion

details:
The need to show one's pronouns in the profile depends on society or language culture. At least in Japan today, that isn't widely known.

As a volunteer UI translator, I want tooltips to explain what this field is for. I'm afraid that people will abandon their original purpose and misuse it.

The most straightforward implementation would be on the "Edit Profile" screen before selecting the pronouns options (see attached image).
title: [1621] need tooltips around the pronouns field

comments.value:
I argree.

I believe this might be used not strictly to pronouns only.

But in any similar way. 

Also, pronouns is not just a hint on how to refer person in the speech, but implicit way to point out gender. In cultures with no strong pronouns, ppl can go straight up "I am a boy", "I am a catgirl" there lmao

And also, even a lot of English users probably going to put something else there, to point something else about their personality.

And so, for example, Japanese ppl can also put latin transliteration of their name into the field or short nickname. 

This is OK and these ideas should be hinted in tooltips.

And must be pointed out the whole purpose of this is to be shown on nameplate for everyone around.

@{5a9fe9983955314156acc4f7|full_name} Although I agree that many users would use this field for alternate uses, rather then the intended purpose, I believe having the official UI suggest alternative uses to the pronouns field might not be suitable in this case. Suggestions of alternate uses might lead to confusion for some users, especially when some cultures will be less aware of the idea of preferred pronouns.

Furthermore, If the official UI states alternate uses for the pronouns field, some users who care about their pronouns might feel uncomfortable.

Current industry standard maintain distinct fields for pronouns and pronunciation for the above reasons, and I believe this should be followed for VRChat. I'm not creating a motion to make a pronunciation field, I dont think it's really necessary, but merging pronunciation into the pronouns field might not be a good decision.

details:
**Summary**

VRCSDK 3.8.1-beta.1 has breaking changes for `IVRCSdkAvatarBuilderApi.BuildAndUpload` that requiring referencing more assemblies than before to access the method.

VRCSDK 3.8.1-beta.1 requires `VRC.SDK3A` assembly to be referenced in addition to `VRC.SDK3A.Editor` and `VRC.SDKBase.Editor`.

This breaks [Upload without preCheck](https://github.com/Sayamame-beans/Upload-without-preCheck) and [VRC Quest Tools](https://github.com/kurotu/VRCQuestTools).

**Description**

VRCSDK 3.8.1-beta.1 added overload for `IVRCSdkAvatarBuilderApi.BuildAndUpload` that has `List<VRCPerPlatformOverride.PlatformOverrideOption>` as a parameter.

The `VRCPerPlatformOverride.PlatformOverrideOption` is defined in `VRC.SDK3A` assembly so the C# compiler requires `VRC.SDK3A` assembly to be referenced to access the `BuildAndUpload` method for overload resolution.

This is a breaking change because `VRC.SDK3A` assembly is not necessary to be referenced in the previous version of VRCSDK.

[This Gist](https://gist.github.com/anatawa12/328b526c942e0e01643283762486e8e0) is the minimum reproducible code to reproduce the issue.

Download zip and extract to the `Assets` folder of Unity project with VRCSDK 3.8.1-beta.1 installed.

It will fails to compile with CS0012 error.

**Possible Solutions**

There is a solution to this problem without bumping the breaking version, and I hope this improves API design of VRCSDK.

That is to add struct similar to `PlatformOverrideOption` into `VRC.SDK3A.Editor` assembly, and copy the contents to `VRCPerPlatformOverride.PlatformOverrideOption` in the `Build` or `BuildAndUpload`.

This will resolve (revert) the breaking changes and will continue to work with existing code.

This shields the internal implementation of PlatformOverride by not exposing the `VRCPerPlatformOverride` component which is currently used for multi-platform build.

By exposing `VRCPerPlatformOverride.PlatformOverrideOption` onto the `[PublicAPI]` surface, it will (partially) expose the fact multi platform build is implemented with component, but it can be changed over the time so designing the API to be flexible is better.

In addition, Developers won't need to write long type name `VRCPerPlatformOverride.PlatformOverrideOption` in their code so this makes code easier to read.

**Additional Notes**

This is not a fatal but `IVRCSdkAvatarBuilderApi.BuildAndUpload` and their properties are not marked as `[PublicAPI]` that should be.
title: [VRCSDK 3.8.1-beta.1] VRCSDK 3.8.1-beta.1 has breaking changes for `IVRCSdkAvatarBuilderApi.BuildAndUpload`

comments.value:
Hey! Thanks for the report

One issue with the proposed solution that I can see is that it would not be able to provide methods for actually assigning overrides (which are currently static methods on the `VRCPerPlatformOverride` class.

Making a shim struct that gets copied over might cause confusion for which one you're supposed to use if you actually want to declare overrides in code and save them on the avatar (without creating a custom storage solution).

So we'd have to also create another API in the SDK editor assembly that expose that (to avoid requiring referencing SDK3A runtime assembly directly).

We're gonna discuss what is the best way forward. But if you have any thoughts on that specific aspect of it - please let me know!

@{61734d8acc7413744089269c|full_name}

> One issue with the proposed solution that I can see is that it would not be able to provide methods for actually assigning overrides (which are currently static methods on the VRCPerPlatformOverride class.

> So we'd have to also create another API in the SDK editor assembly that expose that (to avoid requiring referencing SDK3A runtime assembly directly).

Sorry, I didn’t really check out the new static API in detail.

I think having static methods in the editor assembly with the same struct as the BuilderApi makes sense, like you mentioned.

@{5e4ca2145f9b3726b3b389e7|full_name}anatawa12: got it, thanks!

We're going ahead with making a new class that handles all of these interactions in the VRC.SDK3A.Editor assembly. The class added in beta.1 will be marked internal and used only for the final data storage. All of the interactions would need to go through `PerPlatformOverrides` class.

This also shortens the classname for the options to just `PerPlatformOverrides.Option`

details:
In VRCSDK 3.8.1-beta.2

Client 1628

Udonsharp components with BehaviourSyncMode.NoVariableSync cannot send or receive SendCustomNetworkEvent for public methods with the [NetworkCalling] attribute .

From the Network ID Utility, we have confirmed that a Network ID has been assigned to this object.

The expected behavior for NoVariableSync is to be able to send and receive SendCustomNetworkEvents without having [UdonSynced] variables.

If there is another Udon component with BehaviourSyncMode.Continues or BehaviourSyncMode.Manual, it will be send and receive. This is the expected action.

Currently, if you only want to send and receive SendCustomNetworkEvents, it is useful to set BehaviourSyncMode.Manual. However, if, for example, you want to attach VRCObjectSync together, you have to switch to Continuous. If the author of the script and the user are different, you must leave it at BehaviourSyncMode.Any and let the user of the script decide, which is uncontrollable by the author of the script.

Translated with www.DeepL.com/Translator (free version)
title: BehaviourSyncMode.NoVariableSync works like BehaviourSyncMode.None

comments.value: Could you share a script and hierarchy setup that reproduces this issue? In my testing, a script using `[UdonBehaviourSyncMode(BehaviourSyncMode.NoVariableSync)]` can send events just fine.

@{62b61f8ec938a62475e4cd14|full_name} 

Okay, I created two objects with two Udonsharp scripts and observed what happens when a network event is sent from the Sender to the Receiver.

I was able to send and receive SendCustomNetworkEvent if the receiver side is NoVariableSync. (1st SS)

...and even if the sender is None!

This is at odds with the documentation. What is the correct answer?

https://vrc-beta-docs.netlify.app/worlds/udon/networking/events/#defining-an-event

If the receiver is None, SendCustomNetworkEvent failed to send. This is the expected behavior. (2nd SS)

@{5e8487f1fd13be66cecc227b|full_name}: Ah, I see the confusion! The docs are in fact incorrect here, only the receiver behaviour must not be SyncType None. The sender type is actually irrelevant.

I will adjust the documentation accordingly.

With that in mind, is there still unexplained behaviour or a bug, or does that clear it up?
@{62b61f8ec938a62475e4cd14|full_name}So far it is working as expected. Thank you.
Documentation will be updated.

comments.value:
Also experiencing this issue. What is odd is that i don't have any custom split normal's on the model in blender. The issue is especially apparent in the calves, with this odd wavey pattern.

Avatar ID: avtr_42b0b03b-9241-4c3f-86f9-2fef9a7561c5

World Tested: Default VRC home world.

@{608c3912f10152388b7ad184|full_name}  @{5f04ccd86dd7706aba03bbdf|full_name}  I've looked at your uploaded avatars, and it appears your tangent data is messed up. See attached screenshots. Toon Standard uses tangent data to calculate lighting, including specular, which leads to this result. Usually tangents should be smooth like your vertex normals.

I've adjusted the shader to apply the reflectance value to fresnel regardless, which did appear a bit incorrect, but the root issue comes from this.

@{62b61f8ec938a62475e4cd14|full_name}I’m guessing it’s probably because of Unity recalculating tangents instead of using imported ones? Being completely honest, I have known of tangents but have never understood their function or relation to normals for years

@{62b61f8ec938a62475e4cd14|full_name} Okay quick update. I did change it to imported tangents but that created some more weird lighting. First is with imported tangents and second is with calculated Mikktspace

Edit: Even further digging reveals there isn't really a way to modify tangents within blender. The calculation is mostly done in Unity, which is not good at decoding custom normal tangents.
@{608c3912f10152388b7ad184|full_name}: I believe tangents are calculated from a UV channel somehow?

@{62b61f8ec938a62475e4cd14|full_name} They rely on a myriad of things from what I’ve learned.  UV orientation is a factor, yes,  but not all modeling programs generate tangent data, such as Blender. For reference, none of the UVs on this model are stacked and everything is properly unwrapped (see attached file). However, Unity is trying to generate tangent data based on the custom normals which is throwing off lighting angles greatly. I think a good fix for this would simply (if possible) to make it so that reflectance can be masked out or just doesn’t render on parts of the material that aren’t smooth. As is though, I think this could lead to issues for anyone who uses custom normals since Blender, the most commonly used program to make VRC avatars, does not support tangent editing.

@{608c3912f10152388b7ad184|full_name}:

> just doesn’t render on parts of the material that aren’t smooth

That is, unfortunately, not easy or even possible in a shader. As far as I am aware, most existing community shaders would break down with invalid tangent data as well. I'm not sure this is something that we can fix on our end from a technical perspective.

@{62b61f8ec938a62475e4cd14|full_name} I wonder what exactly causes it then because my models with the exact same custom normal setup have worked fine with Poiyomi, XSToon, Silent Shader, Standard (+ Lite), and others. This is the first example of reflections appearing on a mesh with a smoothness value of 0 for me.

@{62b61f8ec938a62475e4cd14|full_name} Did yet a little more digging and it has something to do with realtime lights it seems. I've provided a couple of pictures, but suffice to say it seems to be adding specular highlights when it shouldn't. I've modified the custom normals of my eye mesh and while it's better, it's definitely not fixed.

The first image shows the inside of the head mesh (namely focusing on the eye cavity and the tongue mesh) with one realtime directional light. There's a specular highlight on the tongue and an erroneous highlight in the eye, where the gloss map specifies it should be completely rough. 

The second image shows the exact same scene, this time with the realtime light disabled.

The third image shows how it looks with a gloss of 0 across the whole mesh and the light is re-enabled.

Something about the reflectance adds glossy highlights to the mesh based on the realtime light even when no gloss should be present at all. Does that help narrow anything down in terms of the issue's source?

@{62ecfd9399e0ce68b3a4da13|full_name} you using the shadow tint at value 1 and shadow boost at 0.3, what do you expect, try lowering it will fix the issue

@{680f1496b78da8b5132f3f14|full_name} As I mentioned before, even when all settings are reset to default, the brightness remains unchanged, so the shadow settings are not relevant. I only attached the material settings just in case. Also, for the record, the emission settings have nothing to do with it either—just to be clear.

@{680f1496b78da8b5132f3f14|full_name} Since you asked what I expect — ideally, I’d like the brightness to be at least closer to ToonLit, because the current Toon Standard is simply too bright. In fact, even ToonLit tends to blow out highlights easily, so it would be best if the shader could avoid overexposure more effectively.

This issue can be divided into two problems.

The first is that there is a difference in Light Probe brightness between the two shaders. Toon Lit calculates the average (which is actually slightly different), while Toon Standard calculates the brightest point, so there is a difference in brightness. I think this is as specified, but I think it would be appropriate for the two shaders to have the same brightness to increase the sense of immersion.

The second is that the brightness of Toon Standard exceeds 1.0. This shader adds a clamped directional light and a light probe. However, the result of adding the two is not clamped, so the brightness will exceed 1.0 and spoil the appearance of the texture. I think this user wants the result of adding the directional light and the light probe together to be clamped.

@{60ffe11e9425ef064dcd9ef5|full_name}: That does make sense, thanks for the investigation!

The brightest-point sampling is indeed intentional, as it tends to give a more toon-style shading in our experience with worlds. I don't expect that part to change.

Clamping the final result instead of the intermediary light calculations might make sense though, and probably solve this issue for most cases. I will look into that!

details:
As is, the Toon Standard shader has the ability to use detail textures and normal maps. The detail albedo can be set to use a variety of blend modes, one of which includes using a mask texture. However, this seems to only impact whether or not the detail albedo uses multiplicative or additive shading.

One feature about Standard Lite that’s really nice is that you can have a universal mask to hide detail textures, both albedo and normal, from any part of the mesh you want. It would be incredibly helpful if a similar setup was added to this shader, as right now there is seemingly no way at all to mask detail normals, which seems like a no brainer given detail normals are usually small tileable textures you only want in specific areas.
title: [SDK 3.8.1-beta.3] Add Mask Input for Detail Normals in Toon Standard

details: Right now, rim lighting on the Toon Standard shader seems to be purely additive. White is bright, black doesn’t render. I propose a drop down that allows us to select what blend mode we’d like for the outline. Two blend modes that would be incredibly useful would be of course multiplicative blending for darker rim lights, but also overlay blending so that we can accentuate and amplify the existing albedo textures by using a color close to white. This kind of behavior would be in line with other toon shaders that have an ‘albedo tint’ slider for their rim light coloration.
title: [SDK 3.8.1-beta.3] Add Blend Mode option for Rim Lighting on Toon Standard

details:
**Behavior**

- When a material using any shader without Ramp, switching to Toon Standard makes Shading "Realistic".

- When a material using any shader without Ramp, switching to Toon Standard (Outline) makes Shading "Custom".

- When a material using Toon Standard (Outline) has "Custom" Shading and no Ramp Texture is set, switching to Toon Standard makes Shading "Realistic".

**Cause**

- When switching shaders used in the material, if some of the material properties are the same as the pre-switch shader defaults and post-switch shader also has default properties for them, Unity uses post-switch shader defaults for them (per properties).

- ToonStandard's default has a Ramp Texture, but ToonStandardOutline or any other shader does not.
title: [3.8.1-beta.4] Shading differs depending on whether shader is switched to ToonStandard or ToonStandardOutline

details:
1. Use something like `NetworkCalling.SendCustomNetworkEvent(NetworkEventTarget.All, nameof(ReceiveNetworkEvent), /* parameters */);`

2. It throws errors because it doesn't convert `NetworkEventTarget.All` and `nameof(ReceiveNetworkEvent)` correctly.

3. This is fixed by deleting `NetworkCalling.` and use `SendCustomNetworkEvent(NetworkEventTarget.All, nameof(ReceiveNetworkEvent), /* parameters */);` directly.

4. The documentation is wrong, or, this is a bug.

```

To trigger a network event, use the SendCustomNetworkEvent method available on UdonBehaviour and UdonSharpBehaviour, or make an explicit call via NetworkCalling.SendCustomNetworkEvent. These are identical and only provided for compatibility.

```

--------

Edit: on close inspection, it appears that`NetworkCalling.SendCustomNetworkEvent` requires the behavior `instance` (i.e. IUdonEventReceiver) input as the first argument (like what the equivalent Udon Graph node is doing/expecting) .

However, `SendCustomNetworkEvent` (without the "NetworkCalling." prefix) no longer requires this argument. The first argument becomes `NetworkEventTarget.All`, and second argument becomes `nameof( /* the custom event */ )`.

Is this intentional?
title: [SDK 3.8.1-beta.4] NetworkCalling.SendCustomNetworkEvent does not interpret arguments 1 and 2 correctly

comments.value: This is intentional, yes. If you call `SendCustomNetworkEvent` without `NetworkCalling.`, you implicitly call it on `this`. This means the first parameter is simply set to the script you are calling it from. Alternatively, you can also have a reference to a different behaviour, and call `reference.SendCustomNetworkEvent` to use `reference` as the "first parameter". The `NetworkCalling.SendCustomNetworkEvent` variant just makes that explicit.

title: [SDK 3.8.1-beta.4] SendCustomNetworkEvent will break if the array an argument contains null

details:
In a previous bug report (https://feedback.vrchat.com/open-beta/p/sdk-381-beta4-toon-standard-has-flickering-nans-on-mobile), I mentioned that the Toon Standard shader has issues with NaNs / intense areas of specular flickering around the edges of meshes when specular is enabled and reflectance is above 0.

This issue has been resolved for materials that have gloss maps secified. Pi stated in the official Discord that this was achieved by multiplying the reflectance by the gloss map. However, if no gloss map is present, the flickering issue reveals itself once more.

comments.value:
In my opinion, the current fallback system doesn’t work well alongside impostors. The main issue is that impostors work per avatar, while fallbacks work per user, which unnecessarily complicates things.

But I wouldn’t remove fallbacks entirely. Instead, my suggestion is to rework them into something like "impostors+". Here's the idea:

- Fallback is uploaded per avatar, as a lightweight version of that avatar.

- The fallback must have Excellent/Good performance, and it cannot contain any custom animators or parameters. It also has to use one of the lightweight standard shaders.

- If a specific avatar has a fallback uploaded, display it instead of an impostor.

What do you think? This approach would prevent the creation of "heavy" fallbacks, while still giving users some control over how they appear to others, without relying solely on impostors.

At the very least, the current Imposter conversion is not pretty. The whole replacement method would be great, but for now low poly is better.

For users with many different costumed avatars, having a representative fallback is easier than Quest conversion. Therefore, I am against abolishing fallbacks while still leaving everything half-baked.

I understand the intention to eventually eliminate fallbacks, but I believe moving forward with removing them in their current state is premature.

At the very least, the current fallback avatars look unappealing and offer no control over their appearance, so I don't feel inclined to use them actively. That said, even with a fallback, it's still possible to represent oneself to some minimal degree.

pinnedComment.value:
We are not planning on implementing loot boxes into VRChat. In VRChat, "Bundles" are packs of items you get together, and have no inherent randomization or "percent droprate" mechanic. They will always contain the same thing for anyone that receives them. There is zero chance or gambling element built into them, and in fact there is no support built into the system for such a mechanic.

These content drops will be first used as a benefit to users that participate in the Pride Charity campaign in June, but will also be leveraged soon as a VRC+ benefit -- every month, you'll get a box full of stuff. Everyone gets the same box, with the same stuff.

VRChat Bundles are a means of delivering content to users without overriding their agency to accept or reject that content.

details:
With the new items system, it would be highly advisable to add the ability to manage which items are shown on a player trust basis using the existing shield system.

By including items as part of the shield system, under "Items" similar to drones, this can allow players to see items from players they can trust, or even limit item visibility to only friends if they so choose.

Additionally, adding "Item Interactions" to shield settings would additionally allow players to manage *whether or not they receive events from items* (such as through contacts¹) regardless of whether or not the item is shown. This would allow players to opt into seeing items without worrying about unwanted interactions from them.

The latter option would be specifically for *receiving* events. As an alternative to adding the latter to the shield system, it could in theory be added similarly to avatar contacts, as an item in the quick menu.

This would increase the safety of the item system as a whole, whilst paving a pathway for safe management and control of user-created items if they are to ever enter into production (TBD).

details:
As VRChat has just introduced its item system, it may still be trying to find its footing and determine what to and not to allow, and how to provide, items going forward.

As part of this, I suggest VRChat add the ability for items to **be marked as "player only".**

What this means is:

- Player-Only Items are *only* visible *to their owner,* **regardless of any safety settings.**

- Player-Only Items may access an additional set of properties of their owner, via Udon & Soba, which may not be available with "public" items.

- Player-Only Items may attach themselves to the player HUD, provide additional utility, interact with the VRC Camera, etc. via Udon & Soba, which most certainly **would not be available to normal items.**

- Player-Only Items **cannot** interact with other players.

The intent of these features would allow VRChat, and potentially users in the event of UGC, to **provide new "utility" items, similar to the VRChat camera or VRC Player Mirror,** which aim to enhance the functionality of the VRChat client.

Existing systems, such as the camera and mirror, could even theoretically be migrated to such an improved system, providing a uniform way of spawning objects, **whether or not they are local to the spawning user.**

Other possible enhancements could be to provide a separate subsection, similar to the "Exclusive" item sections in Stickers & Emoji, for "My Tools", with a subheading of "Visible only to you", where these Player-Only Items would be stored.

details:
Since VRChat has added many cool new dynamically placed objects in the client, as a world creator I would find it very helpful to have more fine-tuned control of "place-able" things.

Currently, world creators can disable portals, items, prints, stickers, drones, pedestals, etc entirely for the entire world.

Instead of blocking these features in the entire world, I would like to use Udon to allow these things in certain contexts, and block them in others.

For example: Allow placing portals and items in the lobby of Murder 4, but prevent these things from being spawned in the game area.

Or: Allow stickers to be placed on a door, but de-spawn nearby stickers when that door swings open.

We already have something similar for the avatar eye height scaling feature. World creators could turn this off for their worlds entirely by editing world details on the website, but in the world itself we can use Udon to allow/disallow scaling dynamically, get any player's height, and set the local player's height directly, and set the allowed range. I would like something similar for all these place-able things, allowing them to be fine-tuned within reason without turning them off entirely. 

Applicable place-able things:

Items, Stickers, Portals, Sharing pedestals

Useful methods to have:

OnItemSpawned --> Tells you the position, rotation, owner

GetAllSpawnedItems --> So you can check their positions, rotations, owners

DespawnItem() --> Pass it something you want to despawn
title: Better control of placing items/portals/stickers with Udon
